articles.content: The streamer, which hasn’t debuted a film at the festival in almost a decade due to France’s strict rules around theatrical releases, is eyeing a return to the south of France in 2027, Variety has learned. Ted Sarandos suggested as much earlier this year, when he told Variety he hoped to “do something special” for Cannes’ 80th edition. Netflix declined to comment. The American gothic mystery, starring Josh O’Connor, Patsy Ferran, Frances McDormand, Lesley Manville and Damian Lewis, was at one point expected to be ready for this year’s Cannes, then Venice, but is now on track for next May. Coen also has a strong relationship with Frémaux, who honored him alongside his brother Ethan at Lyon’s Lumière Film Festival. But there’s a catch. Netflix recently acquired “Jack of Spades,” complicating plans for what would otherwise have been a natural Cannes contender. Under the festival’s rules, all films competing for the Palme d’Or must receive a theatrical release in France. That would trigger the country’s strict windowing regulations, forcing Netflix to wait 15 months before making the film available to French subscribers — something the streamer isn’t prepared to do. And while Cannes would very much like to have Netflix back, it isn’t willing to bend its rules to make that happen. That means the only way for Netflix to return to Cannes with “Jack of Spades” would be out of competition, which has been a deal-breaker for Sarandos. articles.content: James Gray never hid that Jeremy Strong and Anne Hathaway were playing fictional versions of his real-life parents in his 2022 drama “ Armageddon Time, ” based on the writer/director’s experience as a sixth grader growing up in Queens in the 1980s. “Jeremy is doing my father to such a degree that it is disturbing. He sounds exactly like him, looks exactly like him; it’s bizarre. Annie, too, is uncanny about [playing my mother],” said Gray while a guest on this week’s episode of IndieWire’s Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast . “So I had had such a great time with them shooting ‘Armageddon Time,’ I said, ‘Well, why don’t we do this again?’” Related Stories Sean Connery Wasn’t the First James Bond: Meet Barry Nelson in the ‘Casino Royale’ You’ve Never Seen ‘Madden’ Review: David O. Sean Connery Wasn't the First James Bond: Meet Barry Nelson in the ‘Casino Royale’ You’ve Never Seen
articles.content: Ever since George Lazenby first replaced Sean Connery as James Bond in 1969’s “On Her Majesty’s Secret Service,” fans have argued over who makes the best 007 — and those arguments are likely to resume once Robert Pattinson takes the screen as the latest Bond in director Denis Villeneuve’s new iteration. Although Craig has his partisans, Connery tends to be the consensus choice for the best Bond, though I’ve argued here for the merits of 1970s and ’80s Roger Moore. All the Bonds have their virtues, but Connery benefited from being there first — for anyone who discovered the series in its initial heyday, Connery simply is James Bond. Related Stories ‘The Other Bennet Sister’ Christmas Special Trailer: Can Mary Bennet Still Be Herself and ‘the Perfect Wife’? ‘Madden’ Review: David O. Russell Fumbles Again with an Unfunny and Purposeless Football Biopic Yet Connery actually wasn’t the first actor to play Bond. That honor goes to journeyman MGM contract player Barry Nelson , who played Bond in a “ Casino Royale ” adaptation eight years before Connery made the character famous in “Dr. No.” Connery may have been the first 007 to grace the big screen, but Nelson established Bond on the small screen in an episode of the CBS anthology series “Climax!” opposite Peter Lorre in the Le Chiffre role that would later be inhabited by Orson Welles (in the goofy 1967 “Casino Royale”) and Mads Mikkelsen (in the 2006 adaptation that introduced Craig to the series). The 1954 “Casino Royale” is a fascinating artifact that includes elements that would go on to characterize future James Bond movies, while also going in a few other very different directions. The key difference is in the scale, stripped down by necessity for television production. The hour-long “Climax!” episode is all interiors, taking place entirely in the hotel and casino of the title. Movie Theaters Are Back, but the Rest of Hollywood Seems to Be Crumbling

Movie Theaters Are Back, but the Rest of Hollywood Seems to Be Crumbling
articles.content: The pandemic forced many of them to shut their doors for months. When they could finally turn their marquees back on, Omicron and other variants made audiences skittish about returning to cinemas. Then the writers’ and actors’ strikes upended production, leaving them with fewer movies to screen. A promised moviegoing revival kept getting delayed or disrupted , often by circumstances outside of the exhibition industry’s control. At long last, things are finally changing. Domestic ticket sales are up 20 percent year over year, and with potential blockbusters like “Dune: Part Three,” “Avengers: Doomsday,” and “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” on the horizon, analysts expect revenues to easily eclipse $10 billion for the first time since COVID. Grosses in North America currently sit at $8.76 billion through November 15, fueled by franchise fare such as “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “Toy Story 5,” but also by unconventional hits ranging from “Project Hail Mary” and “The Odyssey” to “Obsession” and “You Can See Everything.” Related Stories Desire, Death, and a Breakthrough Year for Queer Cinema ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Review: They Shoot Franchises, Don’t They? Audiences are showing up for superhero movies and three-hour documentaries about a convicted felon. And media companies, which treated the theatrical business as the sick man of the entertainment industry, are finally seeing the value in cinemas, with the likes of Amazon MGM Studios and Skydance committing to making more movies for the big screen than most major studios did over the last decade. Better yet, younger viewers are driving the comeback, with studies showing that Gen Z members are the most frequent moviegoers . That’s the good news. Elsewhere, Hollywood seems to be crumbling. articles.title: Desire, Death, and a Breakthrough Year for Queer Cinema
articles.summary:
Desire, Death, and a Breakthrough Year for Queer Cinema

Desire, Death, and a Breakthrough Year for Queer Cinema
articles.content: A willingness to die for sex is a familiar bargain for queer people. Born in the twentieth century at the wrong place and time? Beware of Nazis, AIDS, and other mortal dangers. Hollywood has at times depicted these threats in ways that emphasize the humanity of LGBTQ+ people, as when Tom Hanks played a lawyer dying of AIDS in “Philadelphia,” during the height of the epidemic in 1993. The industry also has a history of finding ever more creative ways to kill off and scapegoat queer characters, a trope that as recently as 10 years ago seemed to be running amok . But a more twisted and nervy dance between desire and death has unfolded in this year’s spate of particularly macabre queer films. After years of what felt like permanent advances in rights and representation, LGBTQ+ people have been stung by backlash , including attacks on gender-affirming care, legal threats to marriage equality, and cuts to suicide prevention. Amid a reduced perception of safety , anxieties about the possibilities and consequences of nonnormative desire are spilling out onscreen like so much fake blood. Even so, their formulation is evidence of social and creative progress. Related Stories ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Review: They Shoot Franchises, Don’t They? ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ First Reactions: Quentin Tarantino and David Fincher Deliver a ‘Pure Riot’ of a Hangout Movie This alarm has played out, perhaps most obviously, in horror films. In Adrian Chiarella’s “ Leviticus ” and Jane Schoenbrun’s “ Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma ,” same-sex attraction engenders extreme and potentially deadly terror, be it from detractors or the people it consumes. Both films explore not the evils of queerness — an argument that belongs to the tradition of queer-coded villains — but the horrors of having one’s desires villainized. articles.content: Media conglomerate forecasts $26 billion in cash content spending in fiscal 2027, up 9% Disney had a robust quarter, topping Wall Street expectations on the top and bottom lines. But CEO Josh D’Amaro, who’s been in the job for eight months, sees an opportunity for the company to become even more efficient and help fuel future growth. For the three months ended Oct. 3, 2026, which is Disney’s fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the Mouse House reported revenue of $25.95 billion, up 16%, and a doubling of net income to $2.61 billion. Total operating segment income rose 43%, to $4.97 billion. The company reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.77. On average, Wall Street analysts expected revenue of $25.16 billion and adjusted earnings of $1.68 per share, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence. Related Stories UFC 334 Livestream: How to Watch Gane vs. Hokit Online How to Get Last-Minute Harry Styles 'Harryween' Tickets Online Overall, it was a solid quarter across Disney’s entertainment, sports and theme parks businesses. articles.content: Not so long ago, the old it’s-funny-because-it’s-true joke about soap operas was that people in soap operas never seemed to watch soap operas. But now that reality shows have all but taken over that space, the function of soaps has evaporated almost entirely, while “unscripted TV” has absorbed all of its clichés. When it first appeared in 2012, The Hunger Games seemed fresh and even satirical; now, though, it just feels tired, and this sixth lackluster offering raises only one serious question: Hasn’t anyone forced to take part in a violent dystopic game show ever seen a violent dystopic game show before? Aha, you might say. This is a prequel , taking place a full 24 years before the original. True, the citizens of Panem have only had to put up with 49 editions of the Hunger Games thus far, but, leaving aside the ancient art of combat-for-entertainment explored in both Gladiator movies, in our world the idea of films pitting humans against humans has been around since 1932’s The Most Dangerous Game — and we’ve seen it all before, even if they haven’t. articles.content: The European Film Academy will honor multi-award-winning Belgian directorial duo Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne with a Lifetime Achievement Award at its 39th European Film Awards in January 2027. Among the most internationally acclaimed filmmakers to emerge from Belgium and Europe, the brothers have left an indelible mark on European cinema history over the past four decades with their films exploring what it means to live in a society shaped by inequality, migration, and economic pressure. Born in Seraing, in the industrial region of Liège in Wallonia, the landscape and social realities of the region have been an important part of their cinema, providing both the setting and the social environment for many of their films. Related Stories News European Film Awards: 'Fatherland' & 'La Bola Negra' Top Nominations - Full List Of Films & Credits News Hiam Abbass To Receive Honorary European Film Academy Award Jean-Pierre Dardenne studied Dramatic Arts at the Institut des Arts de Diffusion in Brussels, where he was taught by the French playwright and director Armand Gatti. Watch on Deadline Through Gatti, the brothers became involved in filmmaking and started documenting the lives and experiences of people in their local community. Beginning their careers in the late 1970s, the Dardennes established themselves as documentary filmmakers through their production company Dérives, before moving onto fiction. The brothers made their first fiction feature film Falsch in 1987, adapted from a play by René Kalisky about the last surviving member of a Jewish family murdered during the Holocaust. They founded their production company Les Films du Fleuve in 1987. Its early production including The Promise (1996) gave a taste of the distinctive cinematic approach steeped in social issues and authenticity. Set in the industrial world of Liège, it followed Igor, a teenage mechanic’s apprentice whose father is involved in the exploitation of undocumented workers. Three years later, they w

articles.title: ‘NAZA’ Team Sticking To Plan To Release Shattering Documentary On The Guardian Website Within Weeks — IDFA
articles.content: The explosive documentary NAZA has become a worldwide box office sensation, earning $15 million to date. But if co-directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor had prevailed, it might have gone straight from its Venice Film Festival premiere to The Guardian website. “At first me and Rachel thought, let’s put it out online the next day,” Abraham explained as he appeared for a panel discussion about the film at International Documentary Festival Amsterdam ( IDFA ). Their partners on the project convinced the filmmakers that a theatrical release should be part of how NAZA reached viewers. “It’s different audiences,” commented Fionualla Jamison, managing director of sales agent-distributor mk2. “Online — it’s not necessarily everyone who’s going to be aware, who has that viewing habit to go watch something on The Guardian website or on YouTube, depending what people’s setups are. So, we felt it was something that could absolutely exist alongside for different audiences and at cinemas.” Watch on Deadline “Our North Star always has been how we’re going to get this film to people,” said Lindsay Poulton, head of documentaries at The Guardian, who produced the film alongside The Guardian’s Harry Davies and James Wilson of JW Films. “I think sitting in a cinema has been an important part of that. We’ve talked publicly as well about how the film is going to be available on our platform.” Poulton and fellow panelists reiterated The Guardian intends to make the film available for free on its website in early December, although a specific date hasn’t been revealed. In the meantime, the documentary has played theatrically in 50 countries, and recorded a remarkable 1.6 million admissions . Abraham, part of the Oscar-winning quartet of directors of No Other Land , along with Szor, became a believer in the theatrical component. Appearing on the panel by remote from The Guardian offices in London, he said he realized, “The film being immediately accessible doesn’t necessarily translate to

articles.title: ‘Shogun’ Post House SSVFX Hires Jennifer Thompson To Run Studio Operations
articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: Dublin-based post group SSVFX , which has worked on Shōgun and Game of Thrones , has appointed Jennifer Thompson as Head of Studio. Thompson is returning to the Screen Scene Group-owned company, having previously worked there a management consultant and exec producer. She has worked at European VFX studios such as Trixter in Germany, where she was Head of Production, and MPC Film in the UK. She has credits for the likes of The Lion King , Loki and The Suicide Squad . She now joins the 16-year-old SSVFX, which is known for creating complex visual effects. Related Stories News Playhouse Post Opens Doors On Soho Facility After Halo Assets Deal Executives Former Tubi Production Exec Ashla Soter Joins Post House Digital Sword In her new role, Thompson will lead on a new phase of development, look to strengthen international partnerships and drive opportunities across feature film and high-end TV. Watch on Deadline Ireland ‘s VFX industry is attempting to capitalize on the introduction of an enhanced 40% tax credit, which offers qualifying international productions opportunities to undertake large-scale visual effects work in the country. “I’m delighted to return to SSVFX at such an exciting time for the studio and the wider Irish VFX industry,” said Thompson. “I’ve always admired the ambition, artistry and collaborative spirit of the team, and it’s a privilege to be part of its next chapter. She boards a leadership team at SSVFX that also includes VFX Supervisor Donal Nolan, who joined earlier this year and was a former Creative Head of Studio at Milk VFX in Dublin. He leads the studio’s creative operation alongside longstanding SSVFX VFX Supervisor Ronan Gantly, and the team also includes Head of Production Ciarán Keenan. Jake Walshe, CEO of the Screen Scene Group, said: “We are delighted to welcome Jennifer back to SSVFX. She knows our people, our culture and what makes this studio special. Together with Donal, Ronan and Ciarán, we’ve brought together an exc

articles.title: IDA Awards Nominations: ‘Concrete Land’ Lands 6, With ‘To Hold A Mountain’ Close Behind; Elizabeth Holmes Doc In The Mix
articles.content: Concrete Land , which has received little attention in the U.S. so far, surprised with a leading six nominations Tuesday as the 42nd IDA Documentary Awards announced its nominees. Sundance winner To Hold a Mountain came in close behind with five. Concrete Land , directed by Asmahan Bkerat, centers on the the Najar family, “one of the last Afro-Palestinian Bedouin families near Amman,” who face eviction as luxury villas encroach on their land. It won the Grierson Award at the BFI London Film Festival last month but has otherwise largely gone under the radar. Along with Best Documentary Feature, it is nominated for Best Production, Best Documentary Not in the English Language, Best Editing, Best Sound Design, and Best Writing. Related Stories Documentary Oscar Contender 'To Hold A Mountain' To Open In Theaters In December Ahead Of HBO Debut Documentary IDA Documentary Awards Shortlists: 'You Can See Everything,' 'To Hold A Mountain,' 'Nuisance Bear' Make Features Cut, But What Got Snubbed? Joining Concrete Land in the marquee Best Documentary Feature category is To Hold a Mountain , directed by Biljana Tutorov and Petar Glomazić. That film – Montenegro’s choice for the Oscar category of Best International Feature – tells the story of Gara, a remarkable woman who is determined to shield her daughter from harm while simultaneously attempting to prevent the Montenegrin government from turning beloved mountain pastures into a military training ground. Watch on Deadline Also nominated for Best Documentary Feature: A Fox Under a Pink Moon , directed by Mehrdad Oskouei and Soraya Akhlaghi; Rehearsals for a Revolution , directed by Pegah Ahangarani, and You Can See Everything , directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim. The latter film, the box office smash about imprisoned Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, earned three nominations overall, including Best Director and Best Original Music Score, recognizing composer Ari Balouzian. articles.title: Darian Lanzetta Out At Mattel Studios
articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: Darian Lanzetta is out at Mattel Studios , sources tell Deadline. The circumstances surrounding Lanzetta’s departure weren’t disclosed. No next destination was given. Reps for Mattel Studios declined to comment. Lanzetta joined the company as Senior Executive, Film in June 2025 — when toy maker Mattel merged its film and television divisions under the banner of Mattel Studios. During her time there, she worked alongside senior exec Tom McNulty to lead the development and production of films based on Mattel IP. She reported to President and Chief Content Officer Robbie Brenner. Lanzetta spent her entire pre-studio career at CAA, where she helped build Mattel’s filmed entertainment slate, ahead of its big breakout moment with Greta Gerwig’s Barbie . She began her entertainment career as an intern in the agency’s New York office while still a student at NYU before elevating to assistant, trainee and in May 2017, motion picture literary agent. As an agent, Lanzetta worked with writers, directors and producers, both emerging and established, with a focus on championing women and underrepresented artists, generally. Stay tuned for info on where the well-liked Lanzetta lands.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos Describes How Amazon Decided On Robert Pattinson As The Next James Bond
articles.content: If anyone knows the glitzy, globetrotting world of James Bond it’s Bezos, Jeff Bezos . The Amazon founder and world’s second-richest man today revealed that he brought his knowledge of that milieu to the process of choosing the next James Bond, who, if you haven’t heard yet, is Robert Pattinson . “I was heavily involved,” said Bezos at the Semafor Silicon Valley & The World conference today. “We ran a really tight process, and we made the final decision on Friday,” the Amazon MGM Studios overlord revealed. “There were a big group initially, and we down-selected to five finalists, and then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists. Watch on Deadline “It was really interesting. You know: full costume, real sets, other actors with them and three different scenes with each of the five finalists. And then we got together on Friday to spend a couple hours looking at all those screening tests or looking at all of that.” While Bezos said, “all the actors were extraordinarily talented,” Pattinson stood out, even if they initially resisted selecting him. “By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing. But there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances, and it was kind of immediately un-debated. Denis, the director, was…we all sort of gravitated to him. By the way, initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him because he’s already so famous. We sort of thought, maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown. But in the screening tests, it was so obvious: He is James Bond.” . @JeffBezos tells @lizrhoffman he was “heavily involved” in selecting Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond. “Initially, we were slightly biased against him just because he’s already so famous … but in the screen tests, it was so obvious he is James Bond.” pic.twitter.com/xHqnNZ0c1x The The fact that Bezos was involved at all makes me happy Bond is dead,gone, and done. Movie should be boycotted. He is a Trump buddy . P.

articles.content: After a long and thorough search, Amazon MGM Studios has found its next James Bond as Robert Pattinson has landed the coveted role in the next installment in the hit spy franchise. Following the last round of screen tests that Deadline first reported at the end of October, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and director Denis Villeneuve landed on the Primetime star to lead the franchise for Amazon MGM Studios. The process to find the next 007 goes back to the spring, when the studio announced casting director Nina Gold was joining the project and that the search was underway. Following two months of meetings, Deadline reported the first round of auditions would take place in August; since then, the studio, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and director Villeneuve cut the list to its final group and worked out test offers in September. RELATED: James Bond Movies In Order: Filmography, Bond Women & Iconic Villains Watch on Deadline “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime. I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team,” said Pattinson. The final tests were originally planned for earlier in October, but due to schedule conflicts with the finalists, they were pushed to the end of the month so they could happen around the same time. While not confirmed, sources say the group was no bigger than five actors, with Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Nicholas Hoult and Josh O’Connor among the others who would end up testing. Once those were finished, producers and execs took their time with making a decision, ultimately landing on Pattinson for the role. articles.title: Jon Cryer Joins CBS’ ‘Cupertino’ As Judge In Top-Secret Court
articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: Jon Cryer has been set as a guest star on CBS ‘ Cupertino , playing the role of Judge Van Linkerspleen, a federal judge working in a top-secret court. He’s an individual thinker who tries to judge fairly in an environment that only values compliance. Cupertino is a David vs. Goliath legal drama set in the heart of Silicon Valley that follows a lawyer (Mike Colter) who is being cheated out of his stock options by his former employer, a tech start-up. Refusing to back down, he joins forces with another recently fired attorney (Rachel Keller) to represent those taken advantage of by the tech elite and help them fight back in a high-stakes battle against the Goliaths controlling Silicon Valley. Related Stories News 'NCIS: Origins' Sets Gibbs Up For Meeting Across Time In New Teaser As Lala Mystery Intensifies News CBS Midseason Premiere Dates: 'Cupertino' Moves, 'Ghosts' & 'Eternally Yours' Pair Up, 'Sheriff Country' & 'FBI' Slide, 'Survivor' Gets Supersized (Again) The series also stars Ella Stiller, Nik Dodani, Busy Philipps, and Renée Elise Goldsberry. Watch on Deadline “Jon Cryer was perfect, playing a judge you couldn’t tell was a good guy or a bad guy. We needed someone who could deliver the comedy but also dig into the moral dilemma of a judge who needs to follow the law in a deeply flawed system,” shared Robert King and Michelle King, showrunners, co-creators and executive producers of Cupertino . The series airs on Thursdays at 10 PM ET/PT on CBS. Beginning January 17, Cupertino moves to Sundays at 10 to 11 PM. In addition to the Kings, the series is executive produced by Liz Glotzer and Sam Hoffman. Cryer earned two Emmy Awards for his portrayal of Alan Harper on the CBS comedy series Two and a Half Men , first in the Supporting Actor category and then going on to win for Lead Actor. articles.title: Jack McBrayer To Host NBC’s ‘Countdown To Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade’ Featuring Interviews With Leslie Odom Jr & McKenna Grace
articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: NBC is gearing up for the 100th edition of its annual Thanksgiving celebration and will be bringing back the hourlong Countdown to Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade the night before. This year, the special will be hosted by Emmy-nominated actor and comedian Jack McBrayer and feature interviews with parade performers Mckenna Grace and Leslie Odom Jr ., Deadline can reveal exclusively. On the eve of the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade , the countdown special will give audiences an all-access look at the Macy’s Parade Studio to discover exactly what it takes to create the famous floats and balloons prior to their journey through the streets of New York, including the iconic characters making their grand return to the parade after decades away. Creator Taylen Biggs will serve as a special 34th Street correspondent at Herald Square, providing behind-the-scenes coverage of Parade rehearsals on the eve of the 100th march. Watch on Deadline The special will also feature superfans whose lives have been changed by the parade, as well as a preview of the The Divine Nine Unity Step Team’s parade performance. Countdown to Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is produced by Done + Dusted. Katy Mullan and Jim Cantiello serve as executive producers.

articles.title: ‘Only Murders In The Building’ Season 6 Trailer Reveals “The Girl With The Curls” & British Brazzos
articles.content: Hulu ‘s Only Murders in the Building is coming back with its sixth season on Tuesday, December 8, and it’s going to be a big one. Watch the first trailer for Season 6 (above), featuring a slew of the big-name stars who will be part of Charles (Steven Martin), Oliver (Martin Short), and Mabel’s (Selena Gomez) latest adventure tracking down a killer. They include Olivia Colman, Meryl Streep, David Tennant, Nicola Coughlan, Martin Freeman, Jim Broadbent, Jodie Whittaker, Peter Capaldi, Richard Ayoade, Jennifer Saunders, Simone Ashley, Rhea Norwood, Matthew Beard, Sharon Horgan, Richard E. Grant, Geri Halliwell-Horner, Lesley Nichols and Jane Horrocks. Related Stories News TikTok Creator Videos Coming To Disney+ In December As Hulu Integration Takes Full Effect Cancellations and Renewals 'Reasonable Doubt' Gets Early Season 5 Renewal As Season 4 Becomes Hulu Series' Most Watched The show’s Season 6 official synopsis: After successfully bringing the guilty to justice once again, Charles, Oliver and Mabel embark on their hardest case yet when the next victim — Cinda Canning — arrives at their doorstep, summoning them to London to catch her killer. Our beloved trio of true crime-solving podcasters must now navigate their way through the home of the cozy murder mystery, replete with a whole new collection of suspicious and particularly English-eccentric characters. But can they follow in the footsteps of the woman whose podcast started it all for them … without having their story end the same as hers? Watch on Deadline As a refresher, Season 5 ended with a new victim revealed: Cinda Canning (Tina Fey), a legendary true crime podcaster who inspired the show’s core trio. Her final podcast season was titled The Girl With The Curls , a mystery that Cinda found while visiting the U.K. that she explored for her podcast. The woman with the red curls is suspected of murdering a Royal, whom Cinda believes is innocent. Cinda sends her curly-topped subject to the U.S., the only place

articles.title: Disney+ Adapting Bob Mortimer’s Debut Novel ‘The Satsuma Complex’ For TV
articles.content: The debut novel from iconic British comedian Bob Mortimer is being made into a TV show for Disney+ . The Satsuma Complex comes from Tip Toe producer Quay Street , which also made Disney+’s Stolen Girl. The Satsuma Complex follows Gary Thorn, a lonely legal assistant in Peckham, South London, whose life takes a chaotic turn after a chance encounter with a mysterious woman. Following an innocent pint at the local pub with his colleague Brendan, Gary finds himself in a brief, but intense, conversation with the stranger who abruptly vanishes without a trace, leaving behind a book, The Satsuma Complex, as the only clue to her identity. Related Stories News TikTok Creator Videos Coming To Disney+ In December As Hulu Integration Takes Full Effect News Chris Colfer In "Conversation" About 'Glee' Reboot, Jokes He'll Return If Mr. Schue & Sue Perform "WAP" Mortimer is a beloved British comic who most recently made himself a generation of new fans across two seasons of LOL: Last One Laughing. He is one half of the comedy double act Reeves and Mortimer, with past credits including Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing and Shooting Stars. Watch on Deadline Mortimer will create, write and EP the series. No word yet on cast. “I am majorly chuffed and fully carbonated by the news that Gary and his friends and enemies are to be brought to life by Disney+ and Quay Street Productions,” he said. Quay Street boss Nicola Shindler called The Satsuma Complex “unmistakably Bob: brilliantly funny, wonderfully distinctive and full of heart, with a gripping mystery at its centre.” The Satsuma Complex will be EP’d by Shindler for ITV Studios-backed Quay Street. The Hulu Original series was commissioned by Lee Mason, vice president, scripted, and Angela Jain, head of content, Disney+ EMEA. Jain has been given a bigger budget of late. At yesterday’s Disney results, the Mouse House said again it will triple its local originals over the next three years.

articles.title: Paramount+ Drops Trailer For Minnie Driver Heist Drama ‘The Day’; Launch Date Revealed
articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: We’ve got the first footage of Minnie Driver in character as DI Sylvia ‘Vox’ Voxley in Paramount+ ‘s British heist drama The Day . The Emily in Paris and Runaway star is seen in hostage negotiator mode as bank robbers barricaded in a building mid-heist, creating a terrifying siege. The criminals are seen threatening bank staff several times, with one telling Vox they want £100,000 ($132,000) or they “start killing hostages.” The trailer comes as Skydance-owned Paramount announced a December 31 release date for the show, with four episodes launching. The following four debut on January 7, 2027 in all Paramount+ territories bar Germany, Switzerland and Austria. Related Stories News 'Yellowjackets' Co-Creator Bart Nickerson Hints That Unreleased Bonus Episode Didn't Fit "Canon Of The Show" News 'Avatar: Seven Havens' Sets Book 2 Release Date At Paramount+ The series will open from the police perspective and follow the siege through one full day, as Vox battles time and rising pressure to save the hostages. Just as the crisis hurtles towards breaking point, the narrative rewinds and the story is told again from the perspective of the robbers. Each episode flips between the two perspectives, with each shift reframing the truth. Watch on Deadline Luca Pasqualino ( Rivals , The Musketeers ) and Louisa Harland ( Renegade Nell , Derry Girls ) also star the series, which comes from Dynamic Television and Clapperboard Studios , and is based on Jonas Geirnaert and Julie Mahieu’s Belgian series De Dag . Ben Harris and Jesse O’Mahoney wrote the British version. Mike Benson and Andy Morgan are the exec producers for Clapperboard, alongside Daniel March from Dynamic Television, and Tamryn Reinecke. Jake Rollins isp roducer, and Andy Tohill ( The Dig , Dalgliesh ) and Ryan Tohill ( The Dig , Dalgliesh ) co-directed.

articles.title: Harry Styles, Billie Eilish & Sam Fender To Headline Glastonbury 2027
articles.content: Harry Styles , Billie Eilish and Sam Fender are to headline Glastonbury 2027, making them the festival’s youngest headliners of the 21st century. The three solo singers will lead the biggest UK festival, coming after a fallow year in 2026. The 2025 edition was helmed by The 1975, Neil Young and Olivia Rodrigo. Cher will also perform, presumably in the now iconic legends slot on Sunday afternoon. This is former One Direction star Styles’ first-ever headline slot at Glastonbury and is in fact the first time he has played there. It comes off the back of his latest album, “Kiss All The Time. Disco. Occasionally.,” which was paired with a huge tour including 30 dates at Madison Square Garden. Related Stories News BBC Deletes Russell Brand Prison Clip After Playing It "In Error" On 'Today' Show News 'A Passage To India': Ali Fazal, Fiona Shaw & Tom Mison Leading BBC & CBC's TV Reboot Eilish became the youngest-ever Glastonbury headliner in 2022 aged 20 and returns five years on to lead again. Watch on Deadline Like Styles, Fender is headlining for the first time. The rockstar has exploded in popularity of late and his single with Olivia Dean, “Rein Me In,” is now the longest-running number one in UK chart history. With a combined age of just 88, the trio are the youngest Glastonbury headliners of this century. Cher is another buzzy name on the Worthy Farm list, along with the likes of Lily Allen, Massive Attack and Little Simz. This year’s Glasto will prove to be a stern test for the BBC . The 2025 edition devolved into chaos when the broadcaster failed to remove from iPlayer a live stream of controversial rap punk band Bob Vylan, whose lead singer chanted “death to the IDF” and complained about working for a “f***ing Zionist.” The corporation has since bought in a new set of processes and has a new Director General.

articles.title: YouTube Hits Back At Rivals With New Slate Featuring Rising Creators, Established Stars & Hot New Directors
articles.content: As rivals such as Netflix and Disney start encroaching on their world of creators, YouTube has returned fire with a new slate of programming from a slew of burgeoning creators such as Nick DiGiovanni and Emma Chamberlain , established stars including Phil Rosenthal and Aryna Sabalenka and one director that insiders have dubbed the “next Kane Parsons”. The Google-owned streamer held its second annual Creator Premieres event at The Hollywood Roosevelt in Los Angeles, where it unveiled a raft of new titles. DiGiovanni, who is behind the world’s largest food YouTube channel, is launching Chef . The series, which comes from his production company, Knife Drop Studios, is following fellow professional chefs, offering an unfiltered look inside kitchens around the globe after launching the first full length episode Inside the World’s #1 Pizza Restaurant. Chamberlain is launching What Are You Waiting For? Next year. The series, which comes from Amplify Pictures and exec producer Joe Lewis, sees the creator try to understand more about people who wait in line, particularly in New York. Watch on Deadline Last year, Saturday Night Live star Grace Reiter , who also stars on Netflix’s Minimum Wage , launched The Hunger Games (but better) parody. She is following that up with her second unscripted parody film: Twilight (but better) . Produced by But Better Productions, Reiter directs with Andie Schlenker and Anderson Appleby as producers, and Cindy Schlenker as co-producer. Tennis star Aryna Sabalenka is launching Aryna’s Arena: Unfiltered next year. The reality series will follow her as a Gucci ambassador designing her own $250K diamond necklace, a bride-to-be planning a wedding while living out of a suitcase for 300+ days a year and a daughter flying home to Belarus between slams. It comes from UltraBoom Media. articles.title: Jane Lynch On ‘Glee’ Reboot & If She’d Return: “I Would Love To Do Sue Sylvester For The Rest Of My Life”
articles.content: Glee is getting a reboot, and Jane Lynch is open to reprising her role as Sue Sylvester. In a new interview, the Weakest Link host said she would like to play the McKinley High School coach “for the rest of my life.” “If I am asked to partake, the answer will be yes,” Lynch said on The Jennifer Hudson Show about reprising her role. “I cannot wait.” Lynch added, “I would love to do Sue Sylvester for the rest of my life. You know, I wonder, though, how far we can take her now. Because if you look out in the world, there are a lot of Sue Sylvesters out there.” On October 21, Deadline reported that Disney+ and Hulu ordered a Glee reboot, but made no mention on which actors would reprise their roles. Watch on Deadline Deadline recently reported that OG Glee stars Heather Morris and Chord Overstreet were in talks to return to the Glee reboot, after previously reporting that Lea Michele was also in talks to reprise her role as Rachel Berry. Chris Colfer, who played Kurt Hummel, recently teased that he had a “nice conversation” about reprising his role in the revival. “Honestly, at this point, I’m just curious. I don’t have much information about it,” he said on Daily Beast’s Obsessed podcast . “So, I haven’t had a chance to talk to anybody about it, but I recently had a nice conversation with someone, and I’m gonna have more conversations soon.” Colfer continued, “But from what I’ve heard, it sounded very funny, and it sounded like a good idea. So, we’ll see.”

articles.title: Hong Kong Golden Horse Nominee ‘We Are Born Good’ Heads to U.K. With Trinity CineAsia (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.content: Dark comedy “ We Are Born Good ,” which leads this year’s Hong Kong contenders at the Golden Horse Awards with nine nominations, has been picked up for the U.K. by Trinity CineAsia . The distributor secured rights from Edko Films and will open the film in British cinemas on Dec. 4. The film is the feature directing debut of Yeung Leung Chuen, who wrote “Hong Kong Family.” Golden Horse winner Chung Suet Ying (“The Way We Talk”) stars opposite Yeung Wai Lun (“The Sparring Partner”). The supporting cast includes Lo Chun Yip (“Time Still Turns the Pages”), Kearen Pang (“Mama’s Affair”), Ng Wing Sze (“Mad Fate”) and Yan Yuk Yu Amy (Echaluce) (“Night King”). Related Stories 'KPop Demon Hunters' Criterion Collection Blu-ray On Sale for 50% Off on Heels of New Tour Announcement Amazon Debuts $30 Streaming Bundle That Includes Starz, BritBox, AMC+, MGM+ and PBS Masterpiece In One Place At the 63rd Golden Horse Awards, the film is up for best narrative feature, leading actor, leading actress, new director and original screenplay, among other categories. It world premiered at Toronto, then traveled to Zurich for its European bow and Pingyao for its Asian launch. It opened in Hong Kong theaters on Oct. 29. Yeung took his starting point from a CCTV clip that went viral, in which a petty quarrel between a market vendor and a customer turned violent. Rather than dwell on the clash itself, the film digs into what drives people in present-day Hong Kong to snap: money worries, job stress, family duty and social bias, piling up with no release valve. Nobody is painted as a villain. Instead, the story tracks how fury and burnout can tip otherwise decent people into trouble. Zoey, a rising actor drowning in debt, sets out to get even after a restaurant botches her order and refuses to cook a replacement because it’s past closing time. Wing-kat, who runs the place, has his own problems – he’s only just out of prison. What starts as a minor spat becomes a running feud as both their lives

articles.title: Mark Ruffalo, Tilda Swinton, Michael Moore, Barry Jenkins and More Rally to the Defense of Iranian Filmmaker Jafar Panahi
articles.content: The heads of Venice and Berlin film festivals as well as actors such as Mark Ruffalo and Tilda Swinton , and directors like Michael Moore, Barry Jenkins and Alex Gibney are among a host of prominent film players who have rallied to the defense of Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi . A statement shared with Variety , so far signed by 200 individuals or institutions, states that they are “deeply concerned” by reports of the new prison sentence of five years and one month issued by the Tehran Revolutionary Court against Panahi, as well as the confiscation of his assets, the freezing of his bank accounts, a two-year travel ban and a two-year social media ban. Related Stories Here's Where to Get a Sony PlayStation 5 Pro Online, Ahead of the 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Release 'KPop Demon Hunters' Criterion Collection Blu-ray On Sale for 50% Off on Heels of New Tour Announcement It notes that in December, Iran issued a sentence against Panahi of one year in prison and a two-year ban on leaving the country. It adds that in March, Panahi “courageously decided to return to Iran, aware of the risks but having always spoken of his deep love for his country, and for his desire to stay and work there.” The statement, which was instigated by the International Coalition for Filmmakers at Risk in collaboration with a group of filmmaker in the U.S. and Europe, follows a similar letter of protest published by Cannes on Tuesday that said the festival “condemns the judicial persecution of Jafar Panahi and calls for the lifting of all restrictions that prevent him from traveling, creating and expressing himself freely.” Other filmmakers to add their names to the latest statement of protest include Kleber Mendonça Filho, Laura Poitras, Rithy Panh, Lucrecia Martel, Liz Garbus, Asif Kapadia, Jacques Audiard, Olivier Assayas, Roger Ross Williams, Catherine Breillat, Dominik Moll and Abigail Disney, as well as actor-writer-director Arthur Harari. articles.title: Marvel Started Planning for Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom Before Jonathan Majors Was Fired and ‘Avengers: The Kang Dynasty’ Fell Apart, Says Kevin Feige
articles.content: Before “ Avengers: Doomsday ,” there was “Avengers: The Kang Dynasty.” Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige announced the latter title at Comic-Con in July 2022, with Jonathan Majors’ Kang the Conqueror poised to become the Marvel Cinematic Universe’s next Thanos-sized villain starting with 2023’s “Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania.” Those plans, however, were upended a few weeks after “Quantumania” opened in theaters and earned some of Marvel’s worst reviews and box office. Majors was arrested in March 2023 after he assaulted his then-girlfriend in the backseat of a private vehicle. The actor was officially convicted in December 2023, with a six-person jury finding him guilty of two misdemeanor counts of harassment and assault. Marvel did not hesitate to cut ties with him, firing Majors immediately after his conviction was announced. The actor was then sentenced in April 2024 to one year of domestic violence counseling. articles.title: Moshe Rosenthal on Directing Queer Oscar Contender ‘Tell Me Everything’: ‘Certain Films Open a Door in Your Heart for Your Own Memories’
articles.content: Moshe Rosenthal’s “Tell Me Everything” is the story of a father-son relationship fractured by an uncomfortable secret. Set in the late 1980s and early 1990s in Holon, a city in western Israel, it grapples with queerness, masculinity and family just as 12 year-old Boaz is preparing for his Bar Mitzvah. Like all Rosenthal’s work, “Tell Me Everything” (his sophomore effort after “Karaoke”) reflects different facets of his identity. “I don’t want to let it control the story but it’s just there in a way that feels organic and feels honest,” he says, noting there are parallels between his own internal struggles and that of his characters. articles.title: Ali Fazal, Fiona Shaw, Naseeruddin Shah, Tom Mison Lead Richie Mehta’s ‘A Passage to India’ Series for BBC, CBC
articles.content: Ali Fazal (“Mirzapur”), Tom Mison and Fiona Shaw are leading the cast of “ A Passage to India ,” Emmy-winning “Delhi Crime” filmmaker Richie Mehta’s five-part series version of E.M. Forster’s classic novel for the BBC and the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation. Set in the 1920s, the drama follows Aziz (Fazal), a local doctor who has spent years caring for others and who sets out to convince his Indian friends that real friendship with the British can survive colonial rule. His hopes start to come apart after an unexplained episode at the Marabar caves, which leaves him accused of assault. The scandal stirs up violent feeling and builds to a trial that grips the public. As the case plays out, the lives of everyone involved are upended, and Aziz and those closest to him begin to grasp how deeply colonization has shaped them. Mison (“De Gaulle: Resistance,” “See”) plays Fielding, an elusive teacher who becomes close to Aziz. BAFTA winner Shaw (“Bad Sisters,” “Killing Eve”) is Mrs. Moore, a woman who has led a varied life and who comes to India to see her son Ronny (Gwilym Lee, “The Great,” “Bohemian Rhapsody”) and set up a match between him and Adela (Clare Hughes, “Ponies,” “Ten Pound Poms”). Naseeruddin Shah (“Paar,” “The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen”) plays Godbole, who teaches alongside Fielding at his college and offers spiritual grounding as the crisis deepens. Shahana Goswami (“Santosh,” “Four Years Later”) is Amrit Rao, Aziz’s barrister, who has just become India’s first woman lawyer. Danish Hussain (“Haq,” “Tanaav”) plays Hamidullah, Aziz’s uncle and closest friend, who doubts the cross-cultural bonds Aziz believes in. “Adapting ‘A Passage to India’ has been a dream of mine for as long as I’ve been telling stories,” Mehta said. “To reinterpret the complex and intriguing characters that E.M. articles.title: CMA Awards Predictions: Expect Ella Langley to Get Everything but Male Vocalist, and Maybe Even That’s Not Safe
articles.content: Variety is picking the winners for the 2026 CMAs, with plenty of easy-to-place bets on 9x-nominated Ella Langley. But it ain't over till the EOTY sings. The suspense is unbearable: Will the 2026 CMA Awards see Ella Langley enjoying a total sweep, or just a near-sweep? That is a real question, not a rhetorical one. So with best single and best song utterly in the bag, that leaves five more open to see if she can run the board with the Country Music Association’s voters. Entertainer of the Year, especially? There is some real suspense there. In some matters, it does take a crystal ball to see. Here are our predictions for the winners of the 60th annual awards, which air live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena from 8-11 on the east coast and delayed for prime on the west coast, also at 8. But it felt like that was starting to change when Lainey Wilson got it in 2023 without having developed any severe road wrinkles. (She also got it again in 2025.) All of which is to say that there is a question that could be asked with Lainey and this honor: “Too soon?” And the likely answer to that is: “Nope, but thanks for asking.” Still, there is a lane open here for anyone to bust through if voters should decide that an armful of “lesser” awards are good enough for Langley this year. articles.title: ‘The Body’ Creator Quinn Shephard on Quitting Acting and Turning Religious Trauma Into Queer, Catholic Ecstasy
articles.content: At 31, Quinn Shephard is behind some of the most projects about teen girls on television. In 2024, she created Hulu’s subversive true crime series “Under the Bridge,” and on Nov. 11, Netflix released her newest effort: “ The Body ,” a queer psychological drama set at a Catholic high school in 2004 that debuted at No. 3 on the streamer’s weekly viewership rankings. But 20 years ago, her foray into the teen genre began with an unauthorized adaptation of a popular book series that got trapped in development hell. Related Stories Lionsgate Quarterly Revenue Pops 41% on Strength of 'Michael,' TV Series Sales as Studio Narrows Net Loss Meta to Help Bring ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ to 3D Screens — and Its $1,299 VR Glasses “I was trying to make a movie by the time I was 10,” recalls Shephard. “My parents found offer letters that I was writing to, like, my dad’s best friend: ‘Will you play Mr. Scary in my “Junie B. Jones” adaptation?’” But the project “couldn’t get off the ground because we lost the key location,” she says, laughing. (She never remotely considered the possibility that her elementary school principal had been joking when he offered her some classrooms. “I was like, ‘OK, here’s the shooting schedule,’ and he was like, ‘No, I didn’t mean that.’ I was mad ,” she says. “‘Why would you tell me I could?’ I was so fucking annoying. But I don’t think I knew how to be any other way, unfortunately.”) Shephard began her career, and life, as an actress. articles.title: European Lifetime Achievement Award for the Dardenne Brothers
articles.summary: The Belgian filmmakers Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne, two-time Palme d'Or winners, will be honored at the 2027 European Film Awards in January.
articles.content: Sibling directors Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne will be honored with a lifetime achievement award at the 2027 European Film Awards . The acclaimed Belgian filmmakers, two-time Palme d’Or winners for Rosetta (1999) and The Child (2005), will be feted at the 39th European Film Awards in Athens on Jan.16. Over nearly 50 years, with more than a dozen features and a handful of documentaries, the Dardenne brothers have established themselves as the preeminent humanist filmmakers of our time. Their work, finely-honed social dramas about the lives of the marginalised, the impoverished and the vulnerable, most of them shot on location in the industrial town of Seraing, where they grew up, have shaped a generation of filmmakers, in Europe and worldwide. Related Stories Music Harry Styles, Billie Eilish and Sam Fender Set to Headline Glastonbury 2027 TV 'Intimacy on Prescription' Wins Main Prize at Tallinn's TV Beats Co-Financing Market The brothers began as documentarians, recording the lives and experiences of their local community. Those early films helped shape the directors’ later neo-realistic style as well as their enduring commitment to social issues. Rosetta (1999), the story of a turbulent teenager living in a trailer park with her alcoholic mother, trying to hold down any job she can get, premiered at the Cannes Film Festival and won the Palme d’Or for best film. Every Dardenne film since has premiered in Cannes competition. They won their second Palme d’Or for The Child (2005), the story of two young parents on social benefits who sell their newborn baby on the black market. Lorna’s Silence (2008), about a young Albanian woman caught in a deadly citizenship scam, won Cannes’ Best Screenplay honor, as did their most recent feature, Young Mothers (2025) , about a shelter for unwed teenage mums. articles.title: Jeff Bezos Says He Was “Heavily Involved” in Casting Robert Pattinson as James Bond
articles.summary: The Amazon founder told a conference Tuesday that he and the film leadership were initially biased against Pattinson before realizing they found their man.
articles.content: The Amazon founder and chairman told a conference Tuesday that he “was heavily involved” in selecting Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond, working alongside the Amazon MGM leadership team, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman, and director Denis Villeneuve. “We ran a really tight process, and we made the final decision on Friday,” Bezos said at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference. “There were a big group initially, and we selected down to five finalists, and then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists.” By now, those finalists are well known: Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden, Nicholas Hoult, and Pattinson, the man who ultimately secured Bond’s tuxedo. Bezos says that they ran an elaborate screen test, with each actor performing three scenes with full costumes and sets. “They were all amazing, but there was something special about Rob and his performances, and it was kind of immediately un-debated. Denis, the director was, we all sort of gravitated to him,” Bezos recalled. “By the way, initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him just because he’s already so famous. We sort of thought, maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown. But in the screening tests, it was so obvious: He is James Bond.” The casting of Pattinson is without question the biggest move yet by Amazon since it acquired MGM and since it bought out the Broccoli family for control of the franchise. The irony is not lost on people that the Bond franchise is filled with tech tycoons and media industrialists as villains, from Hugo Drax in Moonraker to Max Zorin in A View to a Kill to Elliot Carver in Tomorrow Never Dies . Now James Bond is firmly controlled by one of the world’s richest man, and a mogul whose empire spans tech, media, entertainment and even rockets into space. And this time he was the one helping to call the shots.

articles.title: Bat, Bond and Beyond: How Robert Pattinson Landed 007 (and What Comes Next)

articles.content: Six months of searching for the next James Bond , so many notable actors auditioning, endless media speculation and fan casting, and the winner is … that guy who’s in everything. Robert Pattinson is our seventh 007, and it’s rather tough to criticize Amazon MGM, producers and director Denis Villeneuve for selecting an actor who’s incredibly talented and has shown recent box office appeal. Villeneuve is on record as loving Pattinson’s riveting performance in Primetime , and surely the studio brass had to love that more than 75 percent of the A24 film’s opening-weekend audience cited Pattinson as their main reason for buying a ticket and that Primetime delivered a startlingly high percentage of Gen Z moviegoers (69 percent of the opening-weekend audience was under 30). All of which surely helped Pattinson beat out the diverse pool of rival candidates (and by “diverse,” we mean athletic U.K.-born 36-year-old white guys who are also popular … just not as popular). Plenty of observers note the ways in which the angular, brooding Pattinson has a strikingly different vibe compared to previous Bonds, seeming more like a candidate for the franchise’s villain than its hero. But it’s the actor’s A-list status that most sets him apart from Bond producers traditionally picking an up-and-coming actor who was merely familiar to audiences before putting him in a tux and passing him a Walther PPK. When Amazon MGM took creative control of the James Bond franchise in February 2025 from gatekeepers Barbara Broccoli and her half brother Michael G. Wilson, ending the family’s decades-long stewardship of 007, everybody wondered what a Jeff Bezos-controlled Bond was going to look like. The studio’s previous attempt at a franchise asset landgrab — getting the rights to a Lord of the Rings prequel and releasing two seasons of a good-not-great The Rings of Power TV series — left many skeptical (particularly fanboys who regularly use the word “woke” as a pejorative). So good, and with Denis.” Related Stories Movies Robert Pattinson's Bondmaxxing: How 007 Still Has Pop Culture in a Vice Grip Movies We Now Know What Robert Pattinson Was Doing When the James Bond Casting News Broke Villeneuve also made an appearance at the Los Angeles event to honor Pugh, telling the room at the Four Seasons Beverly Hills that she “belongs to the stratosphere of major movie stars” and has “a rare ability to convey so much inner stillness. She listens with intent and purpose, projecting a deep inner strain, a brilliant intelligence.” During her speech, Pugh reflected on her career and paid tribute to the many who have helped her along the way, saying, “My existence in this job is down to thousands of people.” She also tossed it back to Villeneuve by revealing, “I sent Denis a message this morning, and I said, ‘Congratulations on finding your Bond. Nice catch. Any villains with the size of a five-foot-four female?'” Pattinson’s casting — up against actors including Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Nicholas Hoult — caps years of speculation in Hollywood for who would take over from Daniel Craig as the next 007. “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” said Pattinson in a statement. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya and everyone at Am

articles.title: Penn & Teller Join Short Film ‘The Inspector’ as “Executive Magic Producers” (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The Spanish short is written and directed by Jandro, one of Spain's biggest magician acts.
articles.content: Penn & Teller have pulled off their newest trick, coming on board Spanish short film The Inspector as its “executive magic producers.” The move puts the pair in league with Spanish magician, filmmaker and television personality Jandro, who wrote, directed, and produced the dark comedy thriller, which is seeking to become an Oscar contender this awards season. The parties already worked together when Janto appeared on pair’s magic competition series Fool Us . Penn and Teller will now lend their support and name for the movie’s awards campaign. Related Stories TV The CW Sets Biggest-Ever Summer Lineup With 11 Series TV Alyson Hannigan Joins 'Penn & Teller: Fool Us' as Host Inspector , set in Spain, tells the story of a fraudulent gas inspector who targets vulnerable elderly people, exploiting their trust to gain access to their homes and steal their valuables. His next victim is Carmen, a sweet grandmother with a collection of valuable antiques. He soon gets more than he bargained for. The 12-minute, genre-bending short film combines thriller, mystery and dark comedy. “Jandro, like Hitchcock, understands cinematic sleight of hand. The Inspector is my kind of movie,” said Teller in a statement. “If you like Penn & Teller, you’ll love The Inspector. It’s tricky.” Jandro is one of Spain’s most well-known magicians and one of the most recognizable faces in Spanish television, having spent 15 years as a writer and performer on the popular Spanish late-night show El Hormiguero. He earned fame in magic circles by hoodwinking Penn & teller as part of their Fool Us competition series. He won that contest six times. He also won the award for Spanish Champion of Comedy Magic in his home country. Inspector has already been making its own magic on the festival circuit. The short has played in roughly 200 festivals, winning 50 awards across 22 countries. The film has played at four Oscar qualifying festivals including Sitges in Spain, ShortShorts in Japan, Ireland’s Foyle, and Edmo

articles.title: ‘The Odyssey’ to Receive Ensemble Performance Award at Palm Springs International Film Festival (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Cast members Matt Damon, John Leguizamo and Samantha Morton as well as casting director John Papsidera, who will also be honored with the award, are expected to attend the ceremony.
articles.content: Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey will receive the Ensemble Performance Award at the Palm Springs International Film Festival , the Palm Springs International Film Awards announced on Tuesday. Cast members Matt Damon , John Leguizamo and Samantha Morton , as well as casting director John Papsidera, are expected to attend the ceremony. The Film Awards will take place on Jan. 7, 2027, with the festival running from Jan. 7-18. The Ensemble Performance Award recognizes the “casting director in alignment with the Academy’s newly established best casting award.” Previous recipients include Conclave (2025), King Richard (2022), Mary Poppins Returns (2019), Hidden Figures (2017), The Big Short (2016), The Imitation Game (2015), American Hustle (2014), Argo (2013), The Social Network (2011) and Babel (2007). Related Stories Music Ella Langley Brings Country Into The Grammys' General Field With Seven Nominations Music Grammy Nominations Snubs and Surprises: Harry Styles, Madonna, Noah Kahan Miss Top Nods as Raye, Rosalía Overperform “ The Odyssey is one of the most ambitious films ever made, and its ensemble of performances is nothing short of extraordinary,” Festival chairman Nachhattar Singh Chandi says. “From Matt Damon’s weathered turn as the hero Odysseus, to Samantha Morton’s captivating and terrifying portrayal of Circe, to John Leguizamo’s faithful guidance as Eumaeus, these are just a few of the many performances that bring this world of antiquity to vivid, undeniable life. It is a privilege to celebrate this remarkable company of actors and the casting director who brought them together with the Ensemble Performance Award.” The Odyssey was the first feature film to be entirely shot in Imax. It also stars Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong’o, Jon Bernthal, Charlize Theron and Elliot Page, among others. articles.title: Sundance Institute Partners With Dior to Support Female Filmmakers Through New Initiatives
articles.summary: Ahead of the 2027 festival, the partners announced the creation of a new fellowship for mid-career storytellers, an award for bold new voices, a brunch to celebrate all of the above and an appearance by longtime Dior muse Natalie Portman.
articles.content: In January, the Sundance Film Festival will present its first edition in a new home of Boulder, Colorado, and two months ahead of the anticipated launch, the team has revealed the first VIP guest being welcomed into the fold: Dior . Parfums Christian Dior has officially partnered with Sundance Institute for the purpose of supporting female filmmakers and storytellers. In doing so, they’ve created the Miss Dior x Women at Sundance Institute Award as a way to recognize “a breakthrough cultural force whose bold vision is reshaping the filmmaking landscape.” The honor will be doled out to a talent on the rise as selected by a yet-to-be-announced curated committee and presented by longtime Dior ambassador Natalie Portman during January’s main event. The fellowship, created for “mid-career storytellers who demonstrate artistic excellence and a strong commitment to independent film, will support six artists on their second or third feature film projects through year-round support with direct non-recoupable grants, mentorship, coaching, cohort gatherings, bespoke creative support, networking and a curated Sundance experience. They’ll also get the true Sundance experience beyond Boulder through access to Sundance Institute educational and peer communities via the Artist Accelerator Program, ELEVATE professional development sessions, Sundance Collab opportunities and the Sundance Institute alumni network. But wait, there’s more: the Sundance and Dior initiative launches will be the toast of a new event set to take place during the 2027 film festival — the Women’s Celebration Brunch presented by Dior. articles.title: Film Adaptation of ‘Saint Philomene’s Infirmary for Magical Creatures’ Set from Danny Daneau, Laura C. Lopez
articles.summary: Daneau and Lopez will pen the screenplay for the family film project from Inevitable Studios and Give Not Take Media.
articles.content: Saint Philomene’s Infirmary for Magical Creatures , the middle-grade fantasy novel from Bill Cotter, is getting the feature film treatment from writers Danny Daneau and Laura C. Lopez and producers Inevitable Studios and Give Not Take Media. Rehab Entertainment, Black Bar Mitzvah and independent producer Sydney Foos are also behind the project, which is being planned as a four-quadrant family feature. The story follows a twelve-year-old boy struggling with a new school and a chronic illness who finds a passageway to an enormous subterranean hospital built to care for ailing monsters and magical creatures. He is called upon to help combat a dark force that threatens the peaceful institution. Related Stories Movies Sundance Institute Partners With Dior to Support Female Filmmakers Through New Initiatives Movies 'Hershey' Review: Finn Wittrock Plays the American Chocolate Titan in a Sickly Sweet Biopic Inevitable Studios is the production banner housed within the entertainment and disability-focused Inevitable Foundation. Co-founded by Richie Siegel and Marisa Torelli-Pedevska, the goal of Inevitable Studios is to back film and television that is told through a disability lens. Give Not Take Media is a multimedia entertainment company owned by Caring Across Generations, a national organization focused on caregivers and care recipients, that develops entertainment projects that engage with the experiences of caregiving. Give Not Take Media was behind the recent festival standout Take Me Home , which screened at both Sundance and Tribeca. Terissa Kelton and John W. Hyde‘s Rehab Entertainment recently produced Apple‘s Harriet the Spy and its current slate includes a live-action Disney relaunch of Flight of the Navigator . Black Bar Mitzvah, headed by Jay Ellis and Aaron Bergman, is the production company behind Amazon’s Black Box .

articles.title: Visar Morina on ‘Shame and Money,’ the Kosovo Drama That Won Sundance and Qualified for the Oscars
articles.summary: The director on writing about a village family forced to Pristina, and how worry about his own parents in the pandemic shaped a story of people who are “pawns of politics.”
articles.content: After losing their livelihood in a village, a family in Kosovo is forced to move to the capital, Pristina. But the family struggles “in pursuit of a place in a hyper-capitalist society.” This brief description for director Visar Morina’s ( Exile , Babai ) Shame and Money just teases some of the stresses and challenges its characters face amid a high cost of living. The drama had its world premiere at the Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Dramatic Grand Jury Prize. The award qualifies the film to compete for the best international feature film Oscar under the updated Academy rules. The cast is led by Astrit Kabashi and Flonja Kodheli and also features Kumrije Hoxa, Fiona Gllavica and Alban Ukaj. Related Stories Movies Jeremy Conway, Agent for Anthony Hopkins and Brian Cox, Dies at 87 TV Sharon Horgan to Be the Guest of Honor at CanneSeries Industry Morina co-wrote the script for the vicky bane and Schuldenberg Films production with Doruntina Basha. Janis Mazuch was the cinematographer, while Joëlle Alexis was the editor. The producers are Fabian Altenried, Sophie Ahrens, Kristof Gerega, Pia Hellenthal and Morina. Oscilloscope Laboratories acquired North American distribution rights and is planning to release the movie in early 2027. THR ‘s review called Shame and Money “a tense and crushing view of the global economy through the eyes of a farmer in Kosovo.” The Sundance jury lauded the director for “his powerful and unique portrayal of human dignity in contemporary Kosovo that universally resonates,” calling Morina “a sensitive filmmaker who masterfully draws the audience into the daily struggles of a family [and who has] deep empathy for his characters.” Morina talked to THR about Shame and Money , which is his third film contending for the best international Oscar after Babai and Exile , and how it tells a story that resonates beyond Kosovo – and not only because the film shows a statue of Bill Clinton, which was erected because, as U.S. Preside

articles.title: Skydance Film Re-Org: Kira Goldberg Joins Paramount, Jesse Ehrman Upped to Run Warner Bros.
articles.summary: Goldberg will run Paramount‘s film operations with Don Granger, while Jesse Ehrman will run Warners, with Mikey Ireland remaining as president of production.
articles.content: Skydance is sorting out its film operations at both Paramount and Warner Bros. in the wake of closing its $111 billion acquisition of Warners. Kira Goldberg is leaving Netflix, where she was one of its top film heads, overseeing faith-based, family and young adult films for the streamer. At Paramount, she will oversee film operations with longtime Skydance executive and producer Don Granger as presidents of the motion picture group. Jesse Ehrman , a twenty-year veteran of Warners, has been elevated to president of the motion picture group at the studio. He most recently served as president of production and development. Mikey Ireland, who joined Warners in February after being laid off at Paramount, will remain as president of production at Warners. Warner Bros. has been without a head since Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy were fired last month amid the Skydance merger. The duo had run the studio since 2022, guiding it to a best picture win with One Battle After Another earlier this year and having celebrated hits like Sinners , A Minecraft Movie and Weapons , but seeing a number of their 2026 movies bomb at the box office, most recently the Tom Cruise feature Digger . Elsewhere in today’s announcement was the news that Jeff Goldstein, a 48-year veteran of Warner Bros. who currently serves as the head of global distribution, will be exiting the studio, taking on a consulting role. The execs at Warners and Paramount will all report up to Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg, who oversee all of film for Skydance. The new re-org was done with an eye toward accomplishing the 30-plus movie slate across the two studios and their various divisions, which include New Line and DC Studios, which recently ousted James Gunn and Peter Safran and will install Marvel alum Jeremy Latcham next month. articles.title: ‘Intimacy on Prescription’ Wins Main Prize at Tallinn’s TV Beats Co-Financing Market
articles.summary: "Can good sex save every marriage?" reads a synopsis of the show. "In 1970s Czechoslovakia, two therapists try to prove it."
articles.content: Czech-Slovak drama Intimacy on Prescription won the main prize at the TV Beats Co-Financing Market of Industry@Tallinn & Baltic Event (ITBE) , the market of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF) in Estonia, whose 30th edition runs through this weekend. A total of four awards were handed out to the most promising series projects of the 2026 edition of the event (its sixth in total). The TV Beats Co-Financing Market brought together 10 series projects, originating from Czechia, Estonia, Finland, Lithuania, Ireland, Spain, Belgium, Poland, and Iceland, to be co-developed in collaboration with other European countries. Related Stories Movies European Lifetime Achievement Award for the Dardenne Brothers Music Harry Styles, Billie Eilish and Sam Fender Set to Headline Glastonbury 2027 The main prize is the €50,000 ($55,000) Council of Europe Series Co-Production Development Award. Intimacy on Prescription is directed by Jiří Havelka, written by Kristina Májová and produced by Lukáš Gargulák and Karolina Zalabakova of Cinebonbon. The jury praised the project’s “originality, universal theme, fresh perspective on 1970s Eastern European society and thorough research.” “Can good sex save every marriage?” reads a synopsis of the show. “In 1970s Czechoslovakia, two therapists try to prove it.” Here is more on the series: “An experimental residential sex therapy unit opens inside a psychiatric clinic in Kroměříž. Married couples arrive for a two-week stay hoping to save relationships that have stopped working at home and in bed. Each case begins as a sexual problem, but gradually reveals deeper wounds: shame, power, fear, trauma and the longing to be understood. At the center stand charismatic sexologist František Muller and precise psychologist Petra Tánská, whose methods clash as much as they complement each other. As the clinic becomes an island of openness in a rigid society, the doctors’ own lives begin to fall apart.” Meanwhile, the MIDPOINT Talent Award was present

articles.title: Jane Lynch Is Ready to Reprise Her Role as Sue Sylvester in the ‘Glee’ Reboot
articles.summary: The 'Only Murders in the Building' alum is just the latest original castmember to weigh in on the revival that was officially announced last month with few details as co-creator Ryan Murphy previously shared he'd written a script for the new iteration.
articles.content: “If I am asked to partake, the answer will be yes,” the actress, who played villainous cheerleading coach Sue Sylvester on the Fox series from 2009-2015, said on Monday’s Jennifer Hudson Show . “I cannot wait.” The Only Murders in the Building alum added, “It would be really, really fun to do it again and to get to wear tracksuits every day. That was my most favorite wardrobe.” In fact, if it were up to Lynch, she wouldn’t stop playing the part. Related Stories TV 'Only Murders' Leaves the Building for London in Season 6 Trailer Business Fubo Widens Quarterly Loss on Higher Revenue, Gets to 5.75 Million North America Subscribers “I would love to do Sue Sylvester for the rest of my life,” she told Hudson. “You know, I wonder though how far we can take her now. Because if you look out in the world, there are a lot of Sue Sylvesters out there.” Lynch had previously said in a 2022 Guardian interview that Sue “would be MAGA” and that if the show was on the air today, “I think there would have been people out there who would have wanted to cancel Sue Sylvester.” Disney+ and Hulu officially issued a series order for the Glee revival last month after co-creator Ryan Murphy had been teasing a return of the high school musical in interviews in the months leading up to the announcement, as he was promoting his FX series The Shards and American Horror Story . When the Glee reboot was announced, no producers or castmembers were mentioned, but it’s safe to assume Murphy is involved. 20th Television, which produced the original series, is behind the new show. In August, Murphy told The Hollywood Reporter that he was “considering” bringing back Glee. “For many, many people now in their 20s, they grew up on that show and it meant something to them,” he said. “The music meant something. articles.title: ‘Only Murders’ Leaves the Building for London in Season 6 Trailer
articles.summary: The true-crime podcasting trio's new case takes them across the Atlantic.
articles.content: At the end of Only Murders in the Building ‘ s fifth season, podcaster Cinda Canning ( Tina Fey ) died on the sidewalk in front of the Arconia. But at the moment of her death, Cinda placed her hand across the building’s gate, so as far as Charles ( Steve Martin ), Oliver ( Martin Short ) and Mabel ( Selena Gomez ) are concerned, it counts for purposes of their true crime podcast (also called Only Murders in the Building ). The events leading up to Cinda’s untimely demise, however, took place in London, so the trio heads to England for a new season of the podcast and a chance to take in a new city and new locales.
