And part of who I am is who I surround myself with,” Jay said in a statement. “I couldn’t be happier to work with Hello Party on this. We have such a great collaborative team, and I know we will make something new and unique in the space.” “Music Therapy With Morgan Jay” is developed and produced by Austin-based creative agency Hello Party and financed by Live Nation Studios, which also provides access to its talent roster for guest appearances. “The industry is changing, and agencies that want to stay relevant in the creator economy are going to have to pivot toward actually being creators,” said Ty Stafford, Hello Party’s founder and CEO. “‘Music Therapy’ is proof that branded entertainment can start with a great idea and, with the right partners in place, become something audiences actually want to watch.” “At Live Nation Studios, we’re always looking for new ways to

articles.title: ‘Grendel’ Animated Series Set at Netflix From ‘Widow’s Bay’ Writer Years After Live-Action Adaptation Was Scrapped
articles.content: Netflix has greenlit an adult animated series based on “ Grendel ,” the popular Dark Horse comic book series by Matt Wagner. Serving as showrunner and executive producer is Bobak Esfarjani, who has previously written and produced on “Widow’s Bay,” “Alien: Earth,” “WandaVision” and more. The news comes four years after the streamer scrapped a live-action “Grendel” adaptation it had ordered with Andrew Dabb writing and Abubakr Ali playing the title role. Related Stories Taylor Swift Ties Grammy Record for Consecutive Album of the Year Nominations As CMA Awards Prepare 60th Annual Telecast, Retiring CEO Sarah Trahern Prepares for Her Exit, and Looks Back on Decades of Prime-Time Highlights The official logline for the new “Grendel” series reads, “After the woman he loves is shockingly murdered, Hunter Rose devotes himself to one thing: vengeance. But as he tears through street gangs, the elite and New York City’s supernatural underworld in pursuit of her killer, a chance at a real life forces him to choose: walk away from ultimate power, or become the very monster he hunts.” Alongside Esfarjani, executive producers include Chris Tongue, Tim Wiesch and Jay Komas for Dark Horse Entertainment; Lydia Antonini; and Wagner. Bobbypills is the studio. “It’s incredibly exciting to see my creation finally make this leap to the animated screen!” Wagner said in a statement. “Netflix’s dynamic new series retains the source material’s dark adult themes and also brings a fresh and thrilling approach to the narrative. This is ‘Grendel’ as I’ve always wanted to see the character portrayed — a hyper-kinetic level of action, bracing explosions of violence and a poignant engaging storyline.” “‘Grendel’ has been at the forefront of independent comics for over forty years, and we’re thrilled to bring Matt Wagner’s creation to Netflix,” said John Derderian, vice president of animation series and kids and family TV at Netflix. “Like the comic, this animated series will break the traditional s

articles.title: ‘Ginny & Georgia’ Sets Season 4 Release Date, Drops First Look Photos
articles.content: “Ginny & Georgia” is officially returning to Netflix with a fourth season, promising a series of even more secrets that threaten to be uncovered. Set to release Jan. 21, Season 4 begins with Georgia Miller (Brianne Howey) having dodged a murder charge, and “life is finally back to normal,” per the official description. “Except that the Millers are broke again. And Georgia’s pregnant and doesn’t know who the father is. And strange things keep happening, hinting that maybe Georgia’s past isn’t willing to stay buried. Ginny (Antonia Gentry) is desperate to break the cycle of chaos, and Georgia is desperate to prove to her kids that she can. And as for Austin… well… This season it’s him against the world. The family is at a turning point. But when push comes to shove, will the Millers be able to start fresh? Or will the past pull them back in?” Related Stories Grammy Nominations 2027: Raye Leads With 11 Noms as Rosalía, Olivia Rodrigo, Ella Langley and Other Female Artists Dominate Bill Maher Fires Back at Trump by Comparing Him to Taylor Swift Starring alongside Howey and Gentry in the fourth season are Felix Mallard, Sara Waisglass, Scott Porter, Diesel La Torraca, Jennifer Robertson, Raymond Ablack, Katie Douglas, Chelsea Clark and Nathan Mitchell. Joining the series are Ali Skovbye (“Whistle”), Kataem O’Connor (“40 Acres,” “Murdoch Mysteries”) and Sunny Mabrey (“Cape Fear,” “The Night Agent”). “Ginny & Georgia” is created by Sarah Lampert, who also serves as co-showrunner and executive producer alongside Sarah Glinski. Jenny Daly, Jeff Tahler, Holly Hines, Daniel March (Dynamic Television), David Monahan, Danielle Hoover, Ali Kinney and Lance Samuels and Daniel Iron (Blue Ice Pictures) serve as executive producers.

articles.title: The Time Robert Pattinson Snuck Around Rikers Island (and Why It Could Help Him With James Bond)
articles.summary: Among the actor’s colorful roles is one rather surreal real-life moment in the hoosegow.
articles.content: Amid all the talk of whether Robert Pattinson ’s experiences will allow him to pull off a convincing James Bond , none feel as instructive as the time he went to prison. It was the middle of 2016, and Pattison didn’t commit any crimes, but he badly wanted to be seen as a someone who did. Pattinson was preparing for his role as Connie Nikas, a con on the run, in the Safdie Bros. jangly fugitive-drama Good Time . The Safdies knew some incarcerated people at Rikers, including their friend Buddy Duress, who would go on to be in the film. So, as Pattinson told a reporter writing about the movie in 2017, he begged Josh to get him into the facility. The director obliged, and while inside he and the future James Bond “just kind of went everywhere; we didn’t really ask for permission,” as Pattinson recalled at the time. (The interview was part of a story centered on walking around colorful parts of Queens with the Safdies, a tale in its own right.) The pair got deep inside the infamously locked-down institution, talking to wardens and inmates alike about life on the inside. One interaction in particular stuck with Pattinson. “I had gotten into all this makeup because I didn’t want anyone I met in there to find out who I was or what I was doing; I wanted them to think I belonged. And I thought I was convincing. And then one of the inmates said to me, ‘What are you doing in here? Is it for a scared-straight program?’ [The program to influence innocent-adrift teenagers.] I wasn’t convincing anyone.” “I thought I was looking like some kind of tough guy but he could see right through me,” he continued. (Pattinson is known for telling tall tales in interviews but this one is true — Josh Safdie confirmed the account.) articles.title: Rob Lowe Asked Ben Shapiro to Cast Him in ‘Confession’: “I’ve Worked With Left-Wing Writers. Why Wouldn’t I Work With Right-Wing Writers?”
articles.summary: The Daily Wire founder recently said he told the actor he was "way too handsome" to take on the role.
articles.content: Rob Lowe was ready to sign on to star in Ben Shapiro ‘s Confession after he read the “fantastic” script written by the Daily Wire founder. The Emmy nominee went on the Second Thought podcast Tuesday, where he recounted how he got involved with the film. He started, “I read the script; it was written by Ben Shapiro. I called Ben and said, ‘This is fantastic.’ And he was like, ‘Well, do you think you know anybody 50-ish, leading man who would not be scared just because I wrote it?’ And I go, ‘Yeah, me.’” “And he goes, ‘You’re good with this?’ I said, ‘I’ve worked with the most left-wing writers in the world. Why wouldn’t I also work with the most right-wing writers in the world?’” Lowe added. articles.title: Chris Pratt to Star in Sci-Fi Movie ‘The Traveler’ as He Inks Paramount First-Look
articles.content: Chris Pratt is taking a trip to Paramount . He will star in The Traveler for the studio, where he has also signed a first-look deal. The three-year producing pact could involve starring in projects as well for his Indivisible production banner. The Traveler is based on Joseph Eckert’s novel, which was published over the summer. It’s a father-son story, about a man who is flung through time every morning at 7:52 a.m. The first jump pushes him 24 hours into the future, but every day, the jump doubles in time, meaning soon he’s hurtling years in a single day. His son, meanwhile, grows up to study quantum physics as he attempts to save his father, who has long been missing through time. Related Stories TV Gabriel Luna on How Arnold Schwarzenegger's Christmas Party Led Him to 'The Terminal List' and 'Dexter: Resurrection' TV Kids' Choice Awards: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day,' Zendaya, Tom Holland, BTS Among 2026 Winners Final Destination Bloodlines filmmakers Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein are directing The Traveler from Justin Rhodes’ screenplay. The feature, one of the more original projects on the runway of any major studio, is gearing up to shoot next year. Pratt’s first-look deal, meanwhile, also includes Miami Heat , which has a script from Brad Copeland and has Pratt starring and producing with Hutch Parker. Pratt became an A-list star more than a decade ago with Guardians of the Galaxy , and went on to appear in multiple Avengers movies for Marvel. He also led the Jurassic World franchise from 2015-2022, grossing billions in the process. Earlier this year, he led the animated Super Mario Bros. Galaxy movie, which grossed $1 billion globally, and had a new season of The Terminal List out last month on Amazon. Up next, he stars in Way of the Warrior Kid for Apple TV, which he also produced. The family opens debuts Nov. 25.

articles.title: Blumhouse Atomic’s ‘Sleepover’ to Star Michelle Monaghan, Justin Theroux
articles.summary: Filmmaker Jacob Chase is behind the project, due in theaters next year.
articles.content: Michelle Monaghan and Justin Theroux are packing their sleeping bags for the night. The duo are set to star in Sleepover for Blumhouse Atomic , the movie from Insidious: Out of the Further filmmaker Jacob Chase. The logline is being kept under wraps for the film, which Chase wrote with Night Swim director Bryce McGuire, based on McGuire’s original short story. It’s slated for a wide release from Universal on Oct. 8, 2027, one of eight projects Blumhouse Atomic has in theaters next year. Parker Posey was at one time attached to the project, but revealed last month that was no longer the case. Related Stories Movies Blumhouse Atomic Partners With Horror Comic Creator James Tynion IV for First-Look Deal (Exclusive) Business Jason Blum and James Wan Rename Their Company Blumhouse Atomic’s Jason Blum is producing with Chase and McGuire executive producing. articles.title: Ron Howard Wasn’t Sure He Was the Right Director for ‘Avedon’; This Is What Changed His Mind
articles.summary: The documentary about famed fashion and portrait photographer Richard Avedon premiered on Netflix on Nov. 11.
articles.content: Ron Howard knows his way around a camera: in front of and behind the lens; scripted film or documentary feature. But when his production company, Imagine Entertainment (co-chaired by Brian Grazer), was considering a biodoc on fashion photographer Richard Avedon , Howard wasn’t sure if he should be at the helm. “I really went into it thinking, ‘This is a great subject, it’d be great for Imagine,’” Howard said of the Avedon Foundation opening up the artist’s archives to him during a screening at SCAD Film Festival on Oct. 28. “As I began sort of seeing the breadth of that work, I was immediately impressed, but I still felt like, I’m not sure I’m really the right filmmaker for this, but this is fascinating and I bet we could explore what went on behind the scenes making many of these great photos that we remember.” Related Stories Beyond the Book From Book Club to Netflix: How Katherine Center's 'The Bodyguard' Became 'Guarding Stars' Movies Lee Chang-dong on the Mysteries and Meaning of 'Possible Love' “As I began to do some research, soon I really did connect with it as this very human story that I wanted to tell,” Howard continued. “It was less anecdotal about how photos were done and what glamorous or intriguing figures sat for him, and much, much more about an artist’s journey, and I related to it. In some ways, we’re very different people — he’s an extrovert, I’m not; he was the life of the party, I avoid them — but, man, did he have drive and ambition.” The resulting film, Avedon , now streaming on Netflix , blends commentary from collaborators — former magazine editor Tina Brown, model Lauren Hutton and dancer and choreographer Twyla Tharp — with Richard’s works, both commercial and historic, like his portraits of figures of the civil rights movement. With her parents’ 50th wedding anniversary approaching, they give her a shocking ultimatum: After a lifetime of being protected and supported, Sarah has one month to (finally) leave the family home. articles.title: Nobody Prepared 4DX Audiences for Olivia Colman Having Sex With a Basket
articles.summary: The seat-shaking theater tech is supposed to make audiences feel part of the action. But then came 'Wicker.'
articles.content: The seats move. The wind blows. Water sprays you in the face. That’s 4DX, the movie theater format designed to make audiences feel like they’re inside the action. Usually, that means a chair-shaking car chase or superhero battle. For those watching Wicker , it meant being bucked in their seats every time Olivia Colman had sex with a basket. The dramedy about a fisherwoman who commissions a basketmaker to weave her a husband became the first romance to get the treatment since the format was developed in 2009. Applying that technology to Wicker was “a special case,” says Erik Dane, vp digital marketing at CJ 4DPLEX, the company behind the format, because “in the world of 4DX, there are not that many erotic scenes.” Related Stories Movies 'Wicker' Star Alexander Skarsgard Will Be Pushed Differently for Golden Globes Than Other Awards (Exclusive) Business Alexander Skarsgard to Narrate Quinn Audio Erotica Original Set in World of 'Wicker' Judging by one viewer’s account, they’ve figured it out — even if it’s murder on the janitorial staff. “The seats start thrusting,” posted Tumblr user cranberrymoons in her online review, describing how moviegoers were “covered in the popcorn and diet coke … flying everywhere.” When the onscreen couple broke the bed, the seats jolted along. “My hair is in my face and I’m holding onto the arm rests of my seat trying not to fall out,” she wrote. Afterward came “a beat of stunned silence … while everyone catches their breath.” Then, “the whole room starts cheering and clapping.” The 60 participating theaters sold out for the Oct. 28 event (it was extended through Nov. 4). A Nov. 16 showing of two episodes of Heated Rivalry , HBO’s romance about two gay hockey players, quickly sold out, too. Taz F. Stark used to run the hottest club in London. articles.content: Penélope Cruz, the Oscar-winning actress whose 2026 credits include the Sundance sensation The Invite , Toronto audience award winner La Bola Negra and forthcoming Bunker , has been tapped by the Santa Barbara International Film Festival to receive its Arlington Artist of the Year Award, The Hollywood Reporter can exclusively report. Cruz, the most celebrated Spanish film actress of all time and one of only a handful of Europeans who have become bona fide A-list stars in Hollywood, will collect her award at Santa Barbara’s historic Arlington Theatre on Thursday, Feb. 11, 2027. articles.title: Screen Gems Lays Off Staff as New Leader Comes In (Exclusive)
articles.summary: In October, Sony Pictures hired veteran YouTube executive Fede Goldenberg to lead the division and change its direction.
articles.content: Screen Gems has cleaned house, laying off a majority of its staff as the Sony division enters a new era under its incoming head, former YouTube executive Fede Goldenberg. The division, which specializing in genre movies such as Resident Evil and Underworld and comedies such as Easy A , has let go of senior vp Nathan Samdalh, vp Ellie Walker, and creative exec Peyton Collins, among others, sources tell The Hollywood Reporter . Goldenberg made the cuts and is expected to bring in a new team as he takes Screen Gems in a new direction. The exec was hired in early October and is bringing in a decidedly 2026 focus to the label. Under the new creative strategy, the film label is expanding its longstanding focus on traditional genre films to include theatrical projects from the next generation of so called “digital-native storytellers,” meaning filmmakers who are making names — and gaining followers — in the digital content space à la Curry Barker of Obsession fame and Backrooms filmmaker Kane Parsons. Goldenberg is expected to bring a new team with new roles to implement his digital creator-focused strategy. Ashley Brucks, who had been running the label as president since 2023 , transitioned to a producing role. Samdahl is the former Paramount executive who was instrumental in making the horror hit Smile (and was infamously let go from the studio before the movie became a surprise hit). He also acted as a creative exec at Walter Hamada’s production banner 18hz Productions. He joined Screen Gems in October 2025. Walker was also a former Paramount exec. She joined the Sony division in 2024. Collins was hired in 2024 after working previously at Jeff Robinov’s Studio 8.

articles.title: The Underdog Story Behind the Underdog Story
articles.summary: Fifty years after Sylvester Stallone defied Hollywood’s expectations with 'Rocky,' the film’s unlikely rise from independent production to cultural phenomenon continues to inspire fans to go the distance.
articles.content: When Sylvester Stallone first walked into the offices of producers Irwin Winkler and Robert Chartoff , he was another struggling actor looking for his big break. The producers weren’t casting anything at the time, but as Stallone prepared to leave, he mentioned that he was also a writer. Intrigued, they invited him to send over a screenplay. Although Winkler and Chartoff passed on the initial script, they recognized Stallone’s potential and encouraged him to share whatever he wrote next. A week later, he returned with Rocky . Related Stories Movies 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Powers $31M in Historic Box Office Launch Against Subdued 'Cat in the Hat' Movies Golden Globes: 'I Play Rocky' Submitted as Comedy (Exclusive) “We thought it was really a great script,” Winkler recalled, nearly 50 years after the film’s release. “It was a story about somebody who has very little and believes in himself.” There was just one catch: Stallone insisted on playing the title character himself. “The studios were against it,” Winkler said. “They didn’t want to do the movie in general, and they certainly didn’t want to do it with him. But we persevered, just like he does in the movie.” Inspired in part by the real-life heavyweight bout between Muhammad Ali and underdog Chuck Wepner, the film’s central message was simple: Winning wasn’t necessarily about defeating your opponent, but proving you belonged in the ring in the first place. Working with an approximately $1 million budget, Winkler and Chartoff personally guaranteed the production’s costs, ultimately covering roughly $25,000 in overages themselves. The limited budget also forced the filmmakers to get creative. Take Rocky and Adrian’s romantic outing at the ice-skating rink. articles.title: Nicolas Cage on His Approach to Playing John Madden in New Biopic: “I’m Not an Impressionist”
articles.summary: Cage stars alongside Christian Bale in David O. Russell's 'Madden.'
articles.content: John Madden may be one of the most notable figures in sports history, but he was unknown to Nicolas Cage before the actor portrayed him in new movie Madden . “He was not on my radar. I was growing up watching black-and-white Orson Welles movies and Fellini movies and Bruce Lee. I wasn’t interested in team sports whatsoever,” Cage, a member of the cinema-centric Coppola family, explains. That didn’t stop David O. Russell from casting him in the film , which follows Madden’s journey from a Super Bowl-winning coach to creating the Madden NFL video game and becoming a beloved commentator. Intertwined in that story is Raiders owner Al Davis (played by Christian Bale ), who was Madden’s best friend on and off the field; Russell originally came to Cage to play Davis, which he rejected. Russell That's Strictly for Football Fanatics Movies John Mulaney Teases His 'Get Smart' Reboot: "My Favorite Type of Person to Play" When the director came back with the idea that he play Madden instead, “because I’m someone that likes to stay out of his comfort zone and take a risk, I said yes, because that would be a transformation,” Cage says. “It would be something where I might learn a few things, taking on this character who is really nothing like me.” “That’s what acting’s about. I’m not an impressionist, I’m not [Madden impersonator] Frank Caliendo,” he continues. “I lean more towards being a surrealist, meaning I like to get a concept of a personality and then dig deep and see what I can locate emotionally with my imagination and my psyche and filter it through the cadence and the appearance, within reason, of John Madden. articles.summary: Bella Maclean ('Rivals') and Miss Benny ('Club Kid') also feature in the Tallinn-premiering, Killer Films-backed "non-dependent" movie. Shares Maclin: “There was something special about making this film."
articles.content: Ray Panthaki ( Boiling Point , Colette , Gangs of London ) makes us think about modern culture in his feature directorial debut, In Starland . Clarence Maclin ( Sing Sing ) stars in his, unbelievably, first lead role. The cast also features Bella Maclean ( Rivals ) and Miss Benny ( Club Kid ), among others. Maclin is Ernie, 50, who lives a quiet and unremarkable life – until he becomes involved with online content creators in their 20s. “Finding a place where he finally belongs, Ernie discovers a world of hedonistic pleasure and voyeurism in which every movement he makes begins to blur the boundaries between performance and reality,” reads a synopsis on the website of the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF) in Estonia, where the film celebrates its world premiere on Thursday, Nov. 19. “As he searches for an identity lost in a mysterious past, fractures begin to appear between his newfound friends and the town of which he has been a part of for so long, and Ernie begins to wonder about the cost of his newfound notoriety.” Related Stories Movies He Lives in Madonna's Old Mansion. Jaime Ackroyd is the cinematographer, with editing by Iain Kitching. Le Bateau Lavoir , Archface Films and Christine Vachon ‘s Killer Films produced In Starland . “I haven’t slept properly in years,” Panthaki shares. “But I made a film that I wanted to make with 100 percent creative control. articles.summary: 'Widow’s Bay' producer Bobak Esfarjani will showrun, write and executive produce the series based on Matt Wagner’s dark vigilante creation.
articles.content: The long-running comic book series Grendel is getting a TV series adaptation from Netflix . The streamer announced the upcoming adult animation series on Wednesday as it revealed Widow’s Bay producer Bobak Esfarjani will showrun, write and executive produce. Grendel , created by veteran comics artist and writer Matt Wagner, follows the author Hunter Rose, whose world is turned upside down after the murder of the woman he loves. But as he becomes the revenge-obsessed vigilante Grendel, he faces the choice of whether to return to a more normal life or become something closer to a villain than a hero. While Comico debuted the series in 1982, Dark Horse Comics has recently published the title. “ Grendel has been at the forefront of independent comics for over forty years, and we’re thrilled to bring Matt Wagner’s creation to Netflix,” Netflix’s vp of animation series and kids and family John Derderian said in a statement. “Like the comic, this animated series will break the traditional superhero mold just as Matt’s time-honored comic book has always done. Bobak, Dark Horse Entertainment and Bobbypills are bold storytellers who love this world as much as its fans do, and we’re so excited to partner with them to bring this story to screen.” Netflix’s adaptation of the series will be executive produced by Chris Tongue, Tim Wiesch and Jay Komas for Dark Horse Entertainment as well as Lydia Antonini and Wagner. Bobbypills will serve as the studio. “It’s incredibly exciting to see my creation finally make this leap to the animated screen,“ Wagner added in a statement. “Netflix’s dynamic new series retains the source material’s dark adult themes and also brings a fresh and thrilling approach to the narrative. articles.content: Skydance is making a big move with its TV studios, combining Warner Bros. articles.content: Ruth Bradley, the Dublin-born actress who portrayed the MI5 “head dog” Emma Flyte on the Apple TV spy thriller Slow Horses , will be honored at the Oscar Wilde Awards . The 21st annual event, organized by the US-Ireland Alliance, is set for March 11 at the Ebell in Los Angeles. The party celebrates the work of those from Ireland — and some who are not — who contribute to film, television and music. Actors Jack Reynor and Thaddea Graham also will be feted, and Irish singer Shobsy will perform. articles.title: Taylor Swift Performs Mash-Up of ‘Toy Story 5’ Anthem and ‘Our Song’ at 2026 CMA Awards
articles.summary: The pop star celebrated her return to country’s biggest night with a throwback to the song that made her a country superstar The post Taylor Swift Performs Mash-Up of ‘Toy Story 5’ Anthem and ‘Our Song’ at 2026 CMA Awards appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: The pop star celebrated her return to country’s biggest night with a throwback to the song that made her a country superstar Taylor Swift was feeling nostalgic at Wednesday’s CMA Awards in Nashville, as she incorporated one of her country classics into her performance of “I Knew It, I Knew You.” Swift took the stage at the 60th annual awards show, hosted by Lainey Wilson for the third year in a row, to perform “I Knew It, I Knew You,” which is nomination for single of the year. However, halfway through her performance of the “Toy Story 5” anthem, Swift began rocking out to 2006 country hit, “Our Song.” She was joined onstage by fellow country legend Keith Urban, who played the banjo alongside Swift’s backup singers and band. Additional celebrity cameos included Brad Paisley, Sugarland, Little Big Town, Eric Church, Lainey Wilson and Brooks & Dunn. Wednesday’s performance marks the first time in decade that Swift has attended country music’s biggest night and 13 years since her last performance at the show. Swift received a nomination for “Toy Story 5’s” “I Knew It, I Knew You,” which she produced alongside Jack Antonoff, in the single of the year category alongside Ella Langley’s “Be Her” and “Choosin’ Texas,” as well as Lainey Wilson’s “Somewhere Over Laredo” and Cody Johnson’s “The Fall.” Swift is quite well-decorated with CMA awards, with this year’s single of the year nod marking her 26th CMA nomination. She first attended the show in 2006 and won her first award in 2007 with the Horizon Award. Just two years later, she scored the Entertainer of the Year winner in 2009, and since then has stood as the youngest artist with the honor. By 2013, she was honored with the Pinnacle Award, and was presented the award with Tim McGraw, Faith Hill, George Strait, Brad Paisley, Keith Urban and Rascal Flatts, artists who Swift had previously opened for. articles.title: Rob Lowe Stands by Starring in Ben Shapiro’s ‘Confession’: ‘Why Wouldn’t I?’
articles.summary: “I’ve worked with the most left-wing writers in the world,” the “West Wing” alum adds The post Rob Lowe Stands by Starring in Ben Shapiro’s ‘Confession’: ‘Why Wouldn’t I?’ appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: “I’ve worked with the most left-wing writers in the world,” the “West Wing” alum adds Rob Lowe stood by his starring role in Ben Shapiro’s “Confession” movie, defending that he’s worked with writers on both ends of the political spectrum. During a Tuesday appearance on the “Second Thought” podcast, the “West Wing” alum touched on his lead performance in “Confession,” which was written by Shapiro and released on The Daily Wire’s streaming service. Specifically, Lowe was asked point-blank if he was “worried about doing a movie with a conservative media company.” His answer? “I’m glad you asked this because it’s a really, really, really interesting assessment, of not only where our world is, but where Hollywood is as well,” he said. “I read the script. It was written by Ben Shapiro. I called Ben and said, ‘This is fantastic.’ And he was like, ‘Well, do you think you know anybody, 50-ish leading man who would not be scared just because I wrote it?’ And I go, ‘Yeah, me.’” As Lowe went on, he recalled how Shapiro asked him if he was really “good with it,” prompting the actor to remind the conservative political commentator that he’s “worked with the most left-wing writers in the world.” “Why wouldn’t I also work with the most right-wing writers in the world?’” he recalled telling Shapiro. Despite being a fan of the script, Lowe admitted that “Confession” was a “challenging” and “tough watch.” The film, which also stars James Franco, Jennifer Jason Leigh and Nick Nolte, follows a man, named Alexei, that is arrested in 1930s Moscow and brought to Lubyanka Prison. I see the movies that are picked—we got turned down by every single film festival, summarily frog marched out of any conversation,” Lowe said. “I see what they’re picking up, and it’s all political, right? articles.title: Christina Ricci Reveals Why Cher Hasn’t Spoken to Her for Nearly 30 Years
articles.summary: "She holds a grudge,” the “Yellowjackets” star says of her "Mermaids" co-star The post Christina Ricci Reveals Why Cher Hasn’t Spoken to Her for Nearly 30 Years appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: Christina Ricci revealed that her former “Mermaids” co-star Cher hasn’t spoken to her in nearly 30 years, claiming the music legend and Oscar winner has held a “grudge” over a snub from her youth. The “Yellowjackets” star opened up about her lack of relationship with Cher during Tuesday’s appearance on “Watch What Happens Live,” telling host Andy Cohen that the singer was “still mad at me.” “She holds a grudge,” Ricci said. “Well, when I was 19, I did some Rolling Stone thing and they interviewed her – maybe it wasn’t Rolling Stone, might’ve been Première. But they interviewed her and she said all these things that were not that amazing about me.” As Ricci went on, she noted that Cher, who played her on-screen mother in the 1990 family dramedy that also marked Ricci feature film debut, reached out and left her a voicemail, in which she allegedly accused journalists of trying to get the “worst things” out of her and apologized for the situation. “I was 19. And so, I didn’t return that message,” Ricci said, explaining that she was “pretty sure” Cher was mad at her for never acknowledging the apology. “Because I’ve reached out to her since and have gotten radio silence.” Nonetheless, Ricci maintained that she still “adore[s]” Cher, noting that she even understands why the pop sensation is upset with her. “And I absolutely 100% can imagine being Cher and being like, ‘Oh my god, they misquoted me and I’m going to call this young person and explain to her that they misquoted me,’” she told Cohen. “And the gall of that young person to not return the call and be like, ‘Oh my god, Cher, it’s OK. I love you so much.’ Like, I would be so pissed. I get it.” In “Mermaids,” Cher played unconventional single mother Mrs. Flax, who relocates with her two daughters (played by Winona Ryder and Ricci) to a small Massachusetts town in the 196os. articles.title: Chris Pratt to Star in ‘The Traveler’ Adaptation at Paramount
articles.summary: The adaptation of Joseph Eckert’s novel is part of the actor’s first-look, three-year producing deal with the studio The post Chris Pratt to Star in ‘The Traveler’ Adaptation at Paramount appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: The adaptation of Joseph Eckert’s novel is part of the actor’s first-look, three-year producing deal with the studio Chris Pratt will star in Paramount Pictures’ adaptation of “The Traveler,” based on the novel by Joseph Eckert, The Wrap has learned. “The Traveler” is part of Pratt’s first-look three-year producing deal with the studio through his Indivisible production banner, with the potential to star in select projects. Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein will direct the film based on a screenplay by Justin Rhodes. The film will be produced by Adam Rosenberg and Jules Daly. Additional projects under Pratt’s deal include “Miami Heat,” written by Brad Copeland (“Jerry & Marge Go Large”), with Pratt (“Way of the Warrior Kid”) set to star and produce alongside Hutch Parker (“Venom: The Last Dance”). Pratt has firmly established himself as a global Hollywood powerhouse, with his films collectively earning more than $15 billion at the worldwide box office. Up next, Pratt produces and stars in “Way of the Warrior Kid” for Apple TV, an adaptation of Jocko Willink’s bestselling children’s novel that premieres Nov. 25. He also voiced Mario in “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie,” which opened in April and has grossed more than $1 billion worldwide. Pratt made a highly anticipated return to television with “The Terminal List,” which premiered in July 2022. Based on the Jack Carr novel, the series was produced through his production company, Indivisible Productions, and debuted at No. 1 on Prime Video. It was renewed for a second season, based on Carr’s follow-up novel “True Believer,” which premiered Oct. 21. A prequel series, “The Terminal List: Dark Wolf,” starring Taylor Kitsch, premiered Aug. 27, 2025.

articles.title: How to Watch the 2026 CMA Awards on TV and Streaming
articles.summary: Taylor Swift returns to the show for the first time in more than a decade The post How to Watch the 2026 CMA Awards on TV and Streaming appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: The 60th annual Country Music Awards return this week, and they’re marking the milestone with some massive performances. Among them? None other than Taylor Swift , making her first appearance at the show in 13 years. She’s nominated for her song “I Knew It, I Knew You,” from “Toy Story 5.” So, how can Swifties ensure they don’t miss it? The 2026 CMAs will take place live at the Bridgestone Arena in Nashville on Wednesday, Nov. 18 at 8 p.m. ET. You’ve got a couple of options on this one. If you’d like to watch the awards show via the cable broadcast, you can tune into ABC . If you’d prefer to stream it, you can do that on Disney+. The show will also be available next day on Hulu. Lainey Wilson will host the CMAs this year, marking her third time hosting the event. As always, the CMAs will feature performances from country music favorites. This year, that includes Luke Combs, Vince Gill, Megan Moroney, Mumford & Sons, Chris Stapleton, Lainey Wilson, Stephen Wilson Jr. and more. But, one of the biggest performances of the night will come from the one and only Taylor Swift, who last appeared on the show more than a decade ago. Swift is nominated this year for Single of the Year with “ I Knew It, I Knew You ,” from “Toy Story 5,” marking her 26th career CMA nomination.

Grá mor, Pierce.” Wednesday’s post was not the first time Brosnan has expressed fondness for Pattinson. After playing his father in “Remember Me,” a time that saw Pattinson building upon his blockbuster heartthrob image from the “Twilight” trilogy adaptations, Brosnan told local outlet Irish Central that the young star was navigating overnight fame “very gracefully.” “With Robert Pattinson, I have watched this young lad really acquit himself very gracefully,” Brosnan said at the time. “He’s doing all right with the pressure. He knows what to do and how to do it. It’s a bit overwhelming for him at times. I mean, he really did enter into the vortex of fame with the speed of a flame. So I think he’s got it in control.” The “Remember Me” co-star, 33 years Pattinson’s senior, even compared the “Twilight” actor’s experience to his own with James Bond — little did he know what was to come some 16 years later. “Being in certain films can change you. articles.title: ‘Guarding Stars’ Review: You Didn’t Need This Christmas ‘Bodyguard’ Knockoff, but It’s Fun Anyway
articles.summary: Leighton Meester saves Jared Padalecki from stalkers while pretending to be his girlfriend in Netflix’s likable, romantic riff on the classic '90s thriller The post ‘Guarding Stars’ Review: You Didn’t Need This Christmas ‘Bodyguard’ Knockoff, but It’s Fun Anyway appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: Leighton Meester saves Jared Padalecki from stalkers while pretending to be his girlfriend in Netflix’s likable, romantic riff on the classic ’90s thriller In 1992, a little blockbuster movie called “The Bodyguard” outlined the rules for guarding bodies: Never let them out of your sight, never let your guard down and never fall in love. There were, to be fair, probably a lot more protocols to memorize and presumably a little firearms training, but those were the big three, and you should never, ever break them. Not unless you want to make another a hit movie like “The Bodyguard,” that is, so if we’re being honest, it’s weird that more movies didn’t do it. There are other films about bodyguards who fall in love with their client but not many. It’s a formula with a lot of untapped potential. A clever filmmaker could even make them pretend to be boyfriend and girlfriend at Christmas and get away with it. Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum’s “Guarding Stars” gets away with it. The low-key charming new Netflix Original stars Leighton Meester as a tough-as-nails bodyguard and Jared Padalecki as her annoying movie star client. He just broke up with his Taylor Swift-coded girlfriend, whose brand-new diss track riled her legions of fans into an angry, obsessive mob. He’s got death threats and he needs his body guarded while he visits his family for the holidays. But his mother just got out of surgery and can’t take any stress, so when she assumes the two of them are dating they’re forced to go with it. There’s no trivance quite like a contrivance. “Guarding Stars” has a lot of them, but so do most movies, and nobody gives a damn so long as they’re in the first act. What matters is that two people who hate each other are forced to pretend to be in love, actually fall in love, and eventually Leighton Meester has to chase a homicidal stalker down on horseback. More movies should end that way. If “ Digger ” concluded with Leighton Meester randomly broadsiding Jesse Plemons mid-monologue

articles.summary: Exclusive: Set in New Jersey, Stephanie Ahn’s magical Sundance winner co-stars Son Sukku.
articles.content: The last person Audrey (Moon Choi) wants to share a ride with is Eli (Son Sukku), the other driver in her mother’s car accident. But when the New York physical therapist returns to her childhood home in New Jersey to care for her suddenly injured parent (Won Mi Kyung), Audrey finds herself carpooling with the local security guard — now without a car of his own. Somewhere along the way, she and Eli start looking forward to their next argument. And part of the fun of Stephanie Ahn’s stunning debut, “ Bedford Park ,” is wondering which of them will catch on first. Premiering exclusively on IndieWire, the film ’s official trailer offers a tantalizing glimpse at the buzzy Korean American romance Sony Pictures Classics acquired out of Sundance this past January . “ Bedford Park ” won the festival’s U.S. Dramatic Special Jury Award for Debut Feature and later screened at Toronto and Busan. The production is a true showcase for his longtime collaborator, production visual effects supervisor Andrew Jackson , who began working on the film ‘s elaborate set pieces far ahead of production. “What’s essential is having the visual effects team be part of the main unit through prep, through the shoot, everything — and not treating you guys as somebody that’s going to come on afterwards and add to the film,” Nolan said, speaking with Jackson during a panel following a Visual Effects Society screening of “The Odyssey” at the IMAX auditorium of AMC Theatres’ Universal Cinema location in Los Angeles. articles.summary: Scott vividly portrays "Gandhi" and "Chariots of Fire" star Ian Charleson, who made "Hamlet" his final role at the National Theatre, but the movie around him sinks into forgettability.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on September 5, 2026 during the 2026 Telluride Film Festival. Focus Features will release the film in theaters Friday, November 20.] There’s no question Andrew Scott , the 49-year-old Irish actor, has earned his position as one of the finest contemporary actors going. He’s in demand, but choosing wisely, and in roles that slyly play off his own status as an out gay man (a rare thing indeed) but with something off-center beneath, often a secret. He played Tom Ripley, one even more sociopathic than Matt Damon’s own iconically calculating Adonis, to devastating effect in the sinister Netflix series “ Ripley ,” there more explicitly grappling with the Patricia Highsmith character’s ambiguous (but was it?) sexuality. He played the Hot Priest who turned down a chance at heterosexual, secular love in “Fleabag,” of course, and starred in “All of Us Strangers” as a lonely adult orphan living in a glittering tower, bracing himself for romantic intimacy with Paul Mescal. articles.title: Jim Cummings Wakes Up to a Post-One-Night-Stand Crisis in ‘DISC’ — Watch the Short
articles.summary: Exclusive: Blake Winston Rice directs the short film, which premiered at the 2025 Toronto International Film Festival before screening at over 50 festivals worldwide.
articles.content: It’s rare for a short film to be named one of IndieWire’s favorite movies of the fall festival season. But last year, we couldn’t resist adding “ DISC ” to our roundup of must-see films . Directed by rising filmmaker Blake Winston Rice (who previously made “Tea” with Michael Gandolfini , another short that we championed) and co-written by Victoria Ratermanis, the film premiered at the 2025 Toronto International Film Festival before screening at more than 50 festivals worldwide. Now, just in time for the Best Live Action Short race, IndieWire can debut the full film as this month’s Vimeo Staff Pick. “DISC” stars Ratermanis and indie filmmaker Jim Cummings as two conference attendees whose drunken hookup turns them into unexpected partners in crime when an inexplicable twist of fate turns their world upside down the following morning. We won’t spoil the unique premise, but an official synopsis reads: “After a one-night stand during a work conference, a man and woman wake to an unexpected crisis. With a career-defining presentation looming, the two near-strangers must navigate an uncomfortably intimate situation and the fragile connection it reveals.” Related Stories ‘Artificial’ Trailer: Andrew Garfield Stuns in Luca Guadagnino’s Sharp, Shocking, Funny Portrayal of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman ‘The Comeback King’ Trailer: Glen Powell Is a Cancelled Country Star in Judd Apatow’s Latest Directing Project Following its TIFF premiere, “DISC” went on to play at the 2026 Tribeca Festival, where it reportedly caused audiences to faint in multiple screenings. articles.title: ‘Artificial’ Trailer: Andrew Garfield Stuns in Luca Guadagnino’s Sharp, Shocking, Funny Portrayal of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman
articles.summary: The "Call Me by Your Name" and "Challengers" director takes on artificial intelligence in the Neon release starring Andrew Garfield.
articles.content: Luca Guadagnino takes on — and potentially takes down — artificial intelligence and one of its figureheads with his latest feature film , “Artificial.” A swishy, swively, veering-toward-camp Andrew Garfield plays gay OpenAI CEO Sam Altman opposite an ensemble that includes Oscar-nominated “Anora” breakout Yura Borisov as his former chief scientific officer Ilya Sutskever, Monica Barbaro as erstwhile OpenAI chief technology officer Mira Murati, Ike Barinholtz as an outré Elon Musk, along with Cooper Hoffman, Mark Rylance, Jason Schwartzman, Chris O’Dowd, and Zosia Mamet. Ahead of the film’s release from Neon on Christmas Day, watch the trailer below. Related Stories ‘The Comeback King’ Trailer: Glen Powell Is a Cancelled Country Star in Judd Apatow’s Latest Directing Project ‘Gentle Monster’ Review: Léa Seydoux Learns the Truth About Her Husband in Marie Kreutzer’s Tough Study of Child Sex Abuse Written by former “Saturday Night Live” scribe Simon Rich, “Artificial” dramatizes a two-decade artificial intelligence arms race. AI-pioneering professor Geoffrey Hinton makes a vanguard discovery that will change the course of humanity forever — with Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and more prominent Silicon Valley techbros racing to get in on the vision, inevitably leading to corruption that Guadagnino details with scary prescience. Especially as Ilya falls deeper and deeper under Sam Altman’s frighteningly charismatic sway. As IndieWire’s David Ehrlich previously wrote, “Guadagnino is exploring how difficult it is to abandon the body in the first place — and not just the body, but the intangible essence that it contains. We couldn’t leave it behind if we tried, and this, in his own way, is Guadagnino trying just as hard to do that as Sam Altman ever did.” “Artificial” was something of an industry hot potato for a sizable stint over the summer, with Amazon MGM Studios dropping the film (which it produced) allegedly over its own ties to artificial intelligence and Altman. articles.title: ‘The Comeback King’ Trailer: Glen Powell Is a Cancelled Country Star in Judd Apatow’s Latest Directing Project
articles.summary: Apatow and Powell co-wrote the Universal comedy, which also stars Madelyn Cline and a massive roster of country musicians.
articles.content: A celebrity trying to rebuild their career after a public cheating scandal manages to feel both timely and timeless. The topic is certainly in the news right now, but it’s a safe bet that there will be a similar new scandal when “ The Comeback King ” hits theaters this February. And Universal is hoping that audiences will turn out for a healthy dose of celebrity schadenfreude. Judd Apatow ‘s new film stars Glen Powell as a rising country superstar who happens to be dating the world’s biggest pop icon (Madelyn Cline). But when a snag in their relationship goes public when they start litigating their drama through music — their fans disagree about who cheated on who — he’s forced to step out of the spotlight and rebuild his career from the shadows. Related Stories ‘Gentle Monster’ Review: Léa Seydoux Learns the Truth About Her Husband in Marie Kreutzer’s Tough Study of Child Sex Abuse Tilda Swinton, Mark Ruffalo, Jacques Audiard, and Others Join in Protest of Jafar Panahi’s Prison Sentence “The Comeback King” is the first scripted film that Apatow has directed since his 2022 COVID satire “The Bubble.” Since then he has filled his time directing documentaries about comedy legends including “George Carlin’s American Dream,” “Mel Brooks: The 99 Year Old Man,” and “Paralyzed by Hope: The Maria Bamford Story.” Apatow and Powell co-wrote the film and produce alongside Kevin Misher, Dan Cohen, Barry Mendel, and Josh Church. In addition to Powell and Cline, “The Comeback King” features an eclectic ensemble cast that includes Cristin Milioti, Madelyn Cline, Stavros Halkias, Li Jin Hao, Leanne Morgan, Kumail Nanjiani, Vanessa Bayer, Atsuko Okatsuka, Tig Notaro, Chris Fleming, Mike Birbiglia, and Big Fella. Plenty of country stars also make appearances, including Roll, Brad Paisley, Miranda Lambert, Shaboozey, Chris Stapleton, Brandi Carlile, Luke Bryan, and Reba McEntire. articles.title: ‘Gentle Monster’ Review: Léa Seydoux Learns the Truth About Her Husband in Marie Kreutzer’s Tough Study of Child Sex Abuse
articles.summary: A tough and unflinching social drama about the predators among us — and how difficult it can be to see them for what they are.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on May 15, 2026 during the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. Netflix will release the film on its streaming platform on Wednesday, November 18.] Marie Kreutzer ’s “ Gentle Monster ” opens with virtuoso musician Lucy Weiss ( Léa Seydoux ) sitting at the piano in her Munich apartment and plunking out a stilted but affecting cover of Charles & Eddie’s neo-soul classic “Would I Lie to You?” This is before her Austrian husband Philip (Laurence Rupp) — a documentary TV producer of marginal success — comes home in a burnout panic that spurs them to permanently relocate their family to a cottage in the German countryside. Before the authorities bang on their door with a warrant for Philip’s arrest, forcing Lucy to ride the elevator up to the clearly designated “child porn” floor of the local police station in order to learn the facts of his case. Before she begins to wonder, in rage and terror and desperate layers of self-protective doubt, whether the father of her young son Johnny (Malo Blanchet) might actually be capable of preying on other kids, or even his own. Related Stories Tilda Swinton, Mark Ruffalo, Jacques Audiard, and Others Join in Protest of Jafar Panahi’s Prison Sentence What Happens If We Break Letterboxd? Among other things, this tough and unflinching social drama is a study in how painful it can be for a rhetorical question — like “Would I lie to you, baby?,” for example — to sour into the stomach-churning stuff of an urgent mystery. For the terms of a relationship to change faster than the facts of the matter are able to keep up with, let alone the feelings that might attend to them. “There is no ‘off button’ for pedophilia,” someone explains to Lucy at one point. There isn’t an “off button” for love either. articles.title: What Happens If We Break Letterboxd?
articles.summary: Repertory theaters have been a bright spot in a rough stretch for Hollywood. A possible Letterboxd sale raises concerns about how old movies find new audiences — and what happens if those young cinephiles scatter.
articles.content: Earlier this month, the Trylon in Minneapolis gave audiences six chances over three days to see “Kanał,” Andrzej Wajda’s 1957 film about Polish resistance fighters retreating into the sewers of Warsaw. After opening night, programmer John Moret saw enthusiastic reviews on Letterboxd . Moret could imagine the calculation for somebody still on the fence: “Oh, these people I trust went to go see this movie, and they loved it. And it’s just playing for two more days.” On November 5, the New York Times reported that its parent company was in exclusive talks to buy Letterboxd for roughly $330 million. Under the deal being discussed, the popular film-logging site would likely keep operating on its own but use the Times Company’s advertising technology. Related Stories How GKIDS Home Releases Are Creating the Fandom They Want to See in the World IDA Documentary Awards 2026 Nominations: ‘You Can See Everything,’ ‘Concrete Land,’ and More Earn Nods For theaters like the Trylon, what matters is whether cinephiles who went on opening night can still reach those who might go tomorrow. In 2026, that handoff is working remarkably well on Letterboxd. Five days before “Kanał” opened, Ken Russell’s “The Devils” sold out at the Trylon on election night . Moret also co-founded the national Programmers’ Jam with Bret Berg, theatrical sales director at the American Genre Film Archive, and Dan Halsted of Portland’s Hollywood Theatre. When the Jam met in Los Angeles in May, Berg told IndieWire that programmers had access to more restorations than ever before; plus, more places to show them and a new audience coming through the doors. We helped declare it the Golden Age of Repertory programming this spring. And when we spoke with Berg again this month, he said Letterboxd still drives “the FOMO of needing to be conversant in a movie of the moment.” For at least a few days in Minneapolis, that movie was “Kanał.” Berg can see why a press company might be a good home for Letterboxd.
